+# the Bedrock route's pass-through keys when set in the driver's environment
+# (AWS_REGION AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS_PROFILE AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
+# ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL), and the
+# arm's LOA_* variables (LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false for gates: false).
+# A python3 -I exec shim closes every descriptor above 2 and keeps exactly those keys;
+# values reach it through the environment, never argv, so AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
+# appears in no argv, capture or log (phase-<label>.argv.json records it as "<set>").
+# `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15` bounds the CLI.
+# Container mode (D-4.9, DEC-0411 as amended) runs the same command inside
+#   docker run --rm --name <n> --user <uid>:<gid> --network bridge --read-only
+#     --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=1g --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2
+#     -v <run>/sandbox:/workspace:rw -v <run>/meta/home:/home/evaluser:rw
+#     -w /workspace -e <KEY=value…> -e AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK <image> python3 -I -c <shim> … claude …
+# Exactly two mounts. meta/home/ (mode 0700) holds copies of $HOME/.codex/{auth.json,
+# config.toml} when present and empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store
+# lives there for the whole run, so A6's --resume works across phases. No ~/.claude
+# file is ever copied. The directory is deleted at exit and on interrupt.
+# image_digest = the image's RepoDigest or id (container), else the fingerprint (host).
+# Versions: `fingerprint` is computed from the HOST toolchain; in container mode the
+# toolchain that runs the phases is the image's (Claude Code 2.1.299, codex 0.137.0 by
+# Dockerfile.ablation), so image_digest identifies the batch's versions. On 2026-10-15
+# the host CLI was 2.1.300 while the image pins 2.1.299; every arm runs in the container.
+#
+# Cap and watchdog (D-4.6, D-4.10): while a phase runs the driver re-prices the
+# stream's assistant-turn usage every $LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S seconds (default 1)
+# from per-token prices fetched once per model (pricing.py; $LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON
+# overrides) and SIGTERMs the phase when spent + estimate ≥ the cap (cap_turn
+# recorded). After each phase the result's total_cost_usd (authoritative) plus the
+# sandbox cost-ledger rows written during the phase are added; ≥ cap → cap_failure.
+#
+# Exit codes:
+#   0  finished (any verdict)                                   status completed
+#   1  agent error: a phase exited non-zero or timed out        status agent_error
+#   2  infrastructure: usage, refused arm/type, mount/toggle failure, CLI/docker
+#      or image missing, fixture path rule, leak guard          status infrastructure_error
+#   3  cap failure (run stopped at the cap)                     status cap_failure
+#   4  interrupted (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to the driver, or a phase killed from
+#      outside)                                                 status interrupted
+# pipeline.json is written for every exit except usage errors and --dry-run; it is
+# rewritten with status `running` after each phase so a SIGKILLed driver leaves a
+# record (ablation-row.sh reads `running` as interrupted).
---

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# mount-lib-stub.sh — test stand-in for implementer B's evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh
+# (cycle-130 Sprint 258). pipeline-run.sh sources lib/sandbox-mount.sh by a literal
+# path; pipeline-run.bats (make_harness) and ablation-runs/regen.sh run a temporary
+# copy of the harness with THIS file in that place. Same function names, signatures
+# and return codes as B's contract (0 ok, 2 refused); evidence `key=value` lines go
+# to stdout (the driver appends them to $ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE); the gates toggle writes
+# LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false to $ARM_ENV_FILE as B's library does. The
+# behaviour is deliberately small: copy the prompt tree's .claude/, CLAUDE.md and
+# .loa.config.yaml; apply the toggles the tests check; hash .claude/ with hashlib.
+#   STUB_MOUNT_FAIL=<fn>   make that function return 2 (infrastructure path)
+#   STUB_BRIEF_EXTRA=<s>   appended to task-brief.md (leak-guard cases)
+#   STUB_ARM_ENV_EXTRA=<l> an extra line written to $ARM_ENV_FILE (env filter case)
+
+  _stub_fail init_sandbox_beads && return 2

10	#   review-catch                      REVIEW → AUDIT
11	#   bug-fix | refactor | feature-build PLAN → IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → FIX? → AUDIT → FIX?
12	# A FIX runs only when the gate before it wrote a CHANGES_REQUIRED LOA-VERDICT
13	# trailer (the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` line of
14	# grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md resp. auditor-sprint-feedback.md);
15	# a FIX that does not run is recorded `skipped: true`.
16	# Arms edit the phase set (D-4.2): `sprint_plan: false` drops PLAN; `gates: false`
17	# ends after IMPLEMENT; `loa_mount: false` runs one BARE session (no mount);
18	# `flatline: false` keeps PLAN with the Flatline step off; `context_resets: false`
19	# runs PLAN, IMPLEMENT and FIX as ONE implementer session (`--resume <session_id>`
20	# from the first session's system/init event) while REVIEW and AUDIT stay separate.
21	# The suite's `phase_sets[<review-catch|build>]` and an arm's `phases` override the
22	# default phase list; the toggle edits above apply on top.
23	#
24	# Usage:
25	#   pipeline-run.sh --task-yaml F --arm ID --run-dir D --run-id R --trial N \
26	#                   --source-tree DIR --suite-file F [--max-run-usd 12] \
27	#                   [--executor container|host] [--image IMG] [--claude-bin B] \
28	#                   [--docker-bin D] [--phase-models JSON] [--phase-timeouts JSON] [--dry-run]
29	#
30	# Options:
31	#   --task-yaml F       task.yaml (SDD §3.2); its directory holds TASK.md
32	#   --arm ID            arm id declared in the suite file (`arms[].id`)
33	#   --run-dir D         run directory to create (must not exist or be empty);
34	#                       alias --workspace
35	#   --run-id R          run id recorded in pipeline.json
36	#   --trial N           trial number
37	#   --source-tree DIR   the pinned Loa tree the mount is copied from
38	#   --suite-file F      evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml (read with yq -o=json)
39	#   --max-run-usd USD   per-run cap (default 12; config evals.ablation.run_cap_usd)
40	#   --executor MODE     container (default; DEC-0411) or host
41	#   --image IMG         container image (default loa-ablation:258)
42	#   --claude-bin B      host-mode CLI (default $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
43	#   --docker-bin D      docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
44	#   --phase-models JSON {"PLAN": "<model id>", …} override ($LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS)
45	#   --phase-timeouts JSON {"IMPLEMENT": <seconds>, …} override
46	#   --dry-run           print the phase plan and exit 0; nothing is created
47	#
48	# Run directory layout (DEC-0413 — the grader never reads meta/):
49	#   sandbox/     the agent's tree (its own .git initialised at `base`)
50	#   snapshots/   <label>.bundle + index.json ({IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2: commit}) after
51	#                IMPLEMENT and each FIX
52	#   transcripts/ events-<label>.jsonl (stream-json), stderr-<label>.log
53	#   eval/        model-invoke.jsonl, cost-ledger.jsonl (copied out of
54	#                sandbox/.eval/ after every phase), adversarial-*.json
55	#   meta/        pipeline.json, phase-<label>.argv.json (argv + captured env),
56	#                prompt-<label>.md, arm, arm-evidence.txt, arm-env, refused.json,

64	# CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH
65	# GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GH_CONFIG_DIR=<sandbox/.eval/gh-empty>,
66	# the Bedrock route's pass-through keys when set in the driver's environment
67	# (AWS_REGION AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS_PROFILE AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
68	# ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL), and the
69	# arm's LOA_* variables (LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false for gates: false).
70	# A python3 -I exec shim closes every descriptor above 2 and keeps exactly those keys;
71	# values reach it through the environment, never argv, so AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
72	# appears in no argv, capture or log (phase-<label>.argv.json records it as "<set>").
73	# `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15` bounds the CLI.
74	# Container mode (D-4.9, DEC-0411 as amended) runs the same command inside
75	#   docker run --rm --name <n> --user <uid>:<gid> --network bridge --read-only
76	#     --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=1g --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2
77	#     -v <run>/sandbox:/workspace:rw -v <run>/meta/home:/home/evaluser:rw
78	#     -w /workspace -e <KEY=value…> -e AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK <image> python3 -I -c <shim> … claude …
79	# Exactly two mounts. meta/home/ (mode 0700) holds copies of $HOME/.codex/{auth.json,
80	# config.toml} when present and empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store
81	# lives there for the whole run, so A6's --resume works across phases. No ~/.claude
82	# file is ever copied. The directory is deleted at exit and on interrupt.
83	# image_digest = the image's RepoDigest or id (container), else the fingerprint (host).
84	# Versions: `fingerprint` is computed from the HOST toolchain; in container mode the
85	# toolchain that runs the phases is the image's (Claude Code 2.1.299, codex 0.137.0 by
86	# Dockerfile.ablation), so image_digest identifies the batch's versions. On 2026-10-15
87	# the host CLI was 2.1.300 while the image pins 2.1.299; every arm runs in the container.
88	#
89	# Cap and watchdog (D-4.6, D-4.10): while a phase runs the driver re-prices the
90	# stream's assistant-turn usage every $LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S seconds (default 1)
91	# from per-token prices fetched once per model (pricing.py; $LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON
92	# overrides) and SIGTERMs the phase when spent + estimate ≥ the cap (cap_turn
93	# recorded). After each phase the result's total_cost_usd (authoritative) plus the
94	# sandbox cost-ledger rows written during the phase are added; ≥ cap → cap_failure.
95	#
96	# Exit codes:
97	#   0  finished (any verdict)                                   status completed
98	#   1  agent error: a phase exited non-zero or timed out        status agent_error

105	# rewritten with status `running` after each phase so a SIGKILLed driver leaves a

752

766	        | {from: (.original_model // null), to: (.fallback_model // null), category: (.api_refusal_category // null), scope: (.scope // null)}' \

823	    --argjson ledger_from "$((ledger_before + 1))" --argjson turn_cap_hit "$turn_cap_hit" \

826	    {name: $name, label: $label, skipped: false,
827	     session_id: (if $sid == "" then null else $sid end),
828	     resumed_from: (if $resume == "" then null else $resume end),
829	     model_requested: $model,
830	     models_used: (($result.modelUsage // {}) | with_entries(.value = (.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0))),
831	     effort_requested: (if $effort == "" then null else $effort end),
832	     tokens_in: u("input_tokens"; "inputTokens"), tokens_out: u("output_tokens"; "outputTokens"),
833	     cache_read_tokens: u("cache_read_input_tokens"; "cacheReadInputTokens"),
834	     cache_creation_tokens: u("cache_creation_input_tokens"; "cacheCreationInputTokens"),
835	     cost_usd: ($result.total_cost_usd // ($est_micro / 1000000)),
836	     cost_source: (if $result.total_cost_usd != null then "result" else "watchdog_estimate" end),
837	     ledger_cost_usd: ($ledger / 1000000),
838	     duration_ms: ($result.duration_ms // $dur), wall_ms: $dur,
839	     num_turns: ($result.num_turns // $est_turns), max_turns: $turns, timeout_s: $tsec,
840	     exit: $rc, cli_exit: $cli_exit, timed_out: $timed_out, is_error: (($result.is_error // false) or ($rc != 0)),
841	     result_subtype: ($result.subtype // null), turn_cap_hit: $turn_cap_hit, gate_recovered: $gate_recovered,
842	     refusal_fallbacks: $rf,

844	     ledger_lines_from: $ledger_from,
845	     snapshot: (if $snap == "" then null else $snap end),
846	     verdict: (if $verdict == "null" or $verdict == "" then null else $verdict end),
847	     watchdog: {priced: ($priced != "null"), estimate_usd: ($est_micro / 1000000), turns_seen: $est_turns,
848	                killed: ($killed == 1), cap_turn: (if $killed == 1 then $cap_turn else null end)},
849	     started: $started, finished: $finished}' >> "$PHASES_FILE"
850	
851	  # --- account and decide ---
852	  local cost_micro
853	  cost_micro="$(jq -r --argjson e "${est_micro:-0}" '(.total_cost_usd // ($e / 1000000)) * 1000000 | round' <<<"$result")"
854	  SPENT_MICRO=$(( SPENT_MICRO + cost_micro + ledger_micro ))

856	  if [[ "$killed" -eq 1 ]]; then CAP_PHASE="$label"; CAP_TURN="$cap_turn"; finish cap_failure 3 "watchdog stopped $label at turn $cap_turn"; fi

   echo "Checking System Zone integrity (sha256)..."
   [[ -f "$CHECKSUMS_FILE" ]] || { warn "No checksums file - skipping integrity check"; return; }
 
   local drift=false
-  while IFS= read -r file; do
-    local expected=$(jq -r --arg f "$file" '.files[$f]' "$CHECKSUMS_FILE")
-    [[ -z "$expected" || "$expected" == "null" ]] && continue
+  local submodule_mount=false
+  local not_mounted=0
+  local file expected actual
+  [[ -d ".loa/.claude" ]] && submodule_mount=true
+
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r file expected; do
+    [[ -z "$file" || -z "$expected" || "$expected" == "null" ]] && continue
 
     if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
-      local actual=$(sha256_portable "$file" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+      actual=$(sha256_portable "$file" | cut -d' ' -f1)
       if [[ "$expected" != "$actual" ]]; then
         fail "Tampered: $file"
         drift=true
       fi
+    elif [[ "$submodule_mount" == "true" && -f ".loa/${file}" ]]; then
+      not_mounted=$((not_mounted + 1))
     else
       fail "Missing: $file"
       drift=true
     fi
-  done < <(jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$CHECKSUMS_FILE")
+  done < <(jq -r '.files | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value)"' "$CHECKSUMS_FILE")
 
+  if [[ $not_mounted -gt 0 ]]; then
+    log "not-mounted: ${not_mounted} path(s) exist in the upstream tree but are not linked by this mount"
+  fi
   [[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log "Integrity verified"
+  return 0
 }

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# spend.sh — cycle-130 cycle spend (SDD §5.11, PRD FR-2, DEC-0363)
     4	#
     5	# Prints what the cycle has spent: the run rows' cost_usd plus the operator
     6	# cost ledger's cost_micro_usd since the kickoff timestamp, against the cap.
     7	#
     8	# Usage:
     9	#   spend.sh [--since TS] [--runs FILE…] [--ledger FILE] [--cap USD]
    10	#            [--reserve USD] [--json]
    11	#
    12	#   --since TS     ledger rows with ts >= TS count (default 2026-10-14T13:50:00Z,
    13	#                  the cycle-130 kickoff); run rows are the cycle's own and all count
    14	#   --runs FILE…   run-row files (JSONL, `cost_usd` per row); repeatable, and every
    15	#                  following non-option argument is a file too. Default:
    16	#                  grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/runs.jsonl plus every
    17	#                  evals/results/ablation-2.0/*/rows.jsonl that exists. A row whose
    18	#                  run_id was already counted from another file is counted once.
    19	#   --ledger FILE  cost ledger (JSONL, `ts`, `cost_micro_usd`; default .run/cost-ledger.jsonl)
    20	#   --cap USD      cycle cap (default: evals.ablation.cycle_cap_usd in .loa.config.yaml,
    21	#                  else caps.cycle_usd in evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml, else 1500)
    22	#   --reserve USD  reserve (default caps.reserve_usd in the suite file, else 250)
    23	#   --json         one JSON object: total_usd, runs_usd, ledger_usd, since, cap_usd,
    24	#                  headroom_usd, reserve_usd, runs_files, ledger_file, runs_rows,
    25	#                  runs_rows_deduped, ledger_rows, skipped_lines
    26	#
    27	# Output: cycle spend USD T (runs R + ledger L since S); cap C; headroom H; reserve V
    28	#   headroom = cap - total (negative when over). Default files that do not exist
    29	#   count as zero; a malformed line is skipped and counted (stderr note).
    30	#
    31	# Exit: 0 printed; 1 a named file (or an existing default) is unreadable; 2 usage.

1	     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	     2	# =============================================================================
3	     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
4	     4	#
5	     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
6	     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
7	     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
8	     8	#
9	     9	# Usage:
10	    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
11	    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
12	    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
13	    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
14	    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
15	    15	#               [--max-usd <usd> [--run-cap <usd>]] [--screen [--screen-tasks N]]
16	    16	#
17	    17	# Spend cap (cycle-130 FR-2, SDD §5.5): --max-usd stops launching before the
18	    18	#   next trial when spent + in_flight × run_cap + est_next > max, where spent =
19	    19	#   the executor-reported total_cost_usd of this invocation's completed and
20	    20	#   failed rows, run_cap = --run-cap (default evals.ablation.run_cap_usd in
21	    21	#   .loa.config.yaml, else 12) reserved per running trial, and est_next = the
22	    22	#   mean cost of this arm's completed trials (one task type per recall suite),
23	    23	#   else the pooled mean, else the suite's ab.cost_hint (or cost_hint), else 5.0.
24	    24	#   While the reservation alone blocks the launch it waits for a running trial;
25	    25	#   when spent + est_next > max it cuts: no further launches, running trials
26	    26	#   finish, STATUS.json gets cut_reason: max_usd and cut = {reason, spent,
27	    27	#   in_flight_reserved, max, trials_launched, at_trial}, state partial, exit 1.
28	    28	# Screen (bd-j4lwr): --screen runs one trial of the first N fixtures (default
29	    29	#   2) per arm into <results-dir>/<suite>/screen-<UTC ts>/ (its own MANIFEST,
30	    30	#   STATUS, rows), prints a per-arm table (trials, mean USD, mean recall) on
31	    31	#   stdout, and never writes the suite-level STATUS.json; the suite aggregate
32	    32	#   never reads screen-* batches. --batch and --trials are ignored under --screen.
33	    33	#
34	    34	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
35	    35	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
36	    36	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
37	    37	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
38	    38	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
39	    39	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
40	    40	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
41	    41	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
42	    42	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
43	    43	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
44	    44	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
45	    45	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
46	    46	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
47	    47	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
48	    48	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
49	    49	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
50	    50	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
51	    51	#
52	    52	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
53	    53	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
54	    54	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
55	    55	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
56	    56	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
57	    57	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
58	    58	#
59	    59	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
60	    60	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
61	    61	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
62	    62	#
63	    63	# Executor: Opus 5.5 (DEC-0172, amending D33/DEC-0164): the cycle-129 proof

183	   183	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
184	   184	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
185	   185	verify_corpus() {
186	   186	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
187	   187	import hashlib, os, sys
188	   188	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
189	   189	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
190	   190	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
191	   191	bad = []
192	   192	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
193	   193	    if not line.strip():
194	   194	        continue
195	   195	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
196	   196	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
197	   197	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
198	   198	        continue
199	   199	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
200	   200	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
201	   201	        bad.append(rel)
202	   202	# audit r1 DISS-C-002: a file present on disk but absent from SHA256SUMS is drift too
203	   203	# (the seed's --check already says so; the runner must agree), else an added file
204	   204	# would reach the sandbox under an unchanged corpus digest.
205	   205	listed = {l.split("  ", 1)[1] for l in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip()}
206	   206	walk_root = os.path.join(corpus, only) if only else corpus
207	   207	for root, _d, files in os.walk(walk_root):
208	   208	    for f in files:
209	   209	        rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), corpus)
210	   210	        if rel == "SHA256SUMS" or rel in listed:
211	   211	            continue
212	   212	        if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/")):
213	   213	            continue
214	   214	        bad.append(rel + " (not listed)")
215	   215	if only:
216	   216	    for extra in (f"manifests/{only}.json", "corpus.tsv"):
217	   217	        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(corpus, extra)) and extra not in listed:
218	   218	            bad.append(extra + " (not listed)")
219	   219	    ldir = os.path.join(corpus, "labels")
220	   220	    if os.path.isdir(ldir):
221	   221	        for f in os.listdir(ldir):
222	   222	            rel = f"labels/{f}"
223	   223	            if f.startswith(only + ".") and rel not in listed:
224	   224	                bad.append(rel + " (not listed)")
225	   225	if bad:
226	   226	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
227	   227	    sys.exit(1)
228	   228	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
229	   229	PY
230	   230	}

diff --git a/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml b/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..9df46b07
--- /dev/null
+++ b/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
+#
+# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
+# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
+# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
+# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
+#
+# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
+# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
+# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
+# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
+# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
+# task_types against the known types).
+#
+# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
+#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
+#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
+# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
+#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
+#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
+# =============================================================================
+name: ablation-2.0
+version: 1
+source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
+agy_opt_in: false
+tasks:
+  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
+  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
+  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
+suite_version: 1
+trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
+cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
+caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
+priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
+cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)
+
+# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
+# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
+phase_defaults:
+  models:
+    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
+    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
+    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
+  # REVIEW/AUDIT 60 turns / 30 min: the Sprint 258 smoke saw a review-catch AUDIT hit 40 turns after writing its
+  # verdict (DEC-0490); BARE stays the implementer-side sum (PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX)
+  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 60, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 60, BARE: 170}
+  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 30, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 30, BARE: 70}
+  tools: "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"   # identical for every arm, A0 included
+phase_sets:   # D-4.1: A1's phases per task type; FIX runs only after a CHANGES_REQUIRED gate
+  review-catch: [REVIEW, AUDIT]
+  build: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX]
+
+arms:
+  - {id: a0_bare, label: A0, task_types: [all], toggles: {loa_mount: false}, phases: [BARE], effort: high,
+     took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a1_full, label: A1, task_types: [all], toggles: {}, took_effect: [all_phases_present, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a2_no_sprint_plan, label: A2, task_types: [build], toggles: {sprint_plan: false},
+     phases: [IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX],
+     took_effect: [no_plan_phase, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a3_one_voice, label: A3, task_types: [all], toggles: {companion_voice: false}, took_effect: [one_voice_planned, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a4_no_gates, label: A4, task_types: [build], toggles: {gates: false},
+     phases: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT],
+     took_effect: [no_gate_phases, enforce_env_false, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}   # build only: on a review-catch task the gates are the task (DEC-0400)
+  - {id: a5_no_flatline, label: A5, task_types: [build], toggles: {flatline: false},
+     took_effect: [no_flatline_rows, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a6_one_window, label: A6, task_types: [build], toggles: {context_resets: false},
+     took_effect: [implementer_single_session, gates_separate_sessions, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a7_effort_medium, label: A7, task_types: [all], toggles: {effort: medium},
+     took_effect: [effort_flag_medium, skill_effort_stripped, integrity_clean]}
+  - {id: a8_no_ceremonies, label: A8, absent: true,
+     evidence: "no /meeting command, skill or sosyete config key at 4d69c3c4 (grep -rli sosyete .claude/ docs/; ls .claude/commands .claude/skills)"}
+
+rules:   # D-A5: pre-registered, mirrored in NOTES
+  threshold_points: 0.03
+  cost_lower_pct: 15
+  bootstrap: {resamples: 10000, level: 0.90, paired: true, units: {hidden_test_pass_rate: tasks, defect_catch_rate: defects}, also_report: {defect_catch_rate: tasks}}   # DEC-0399
+  primaries_by_arm: {build_only: [hidden_test_pass_rate], all_types: [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate]}   # DEC-0400
+  cap_failure: counts_as_failed            # 0 on each applicable primary (DEC-0393)
+  exclusion: {statuses: [degraded, contaminated, interrupted], mode: pairwise, inconclusive_above_share: 0.25}
+  sensitivity_figure: cap_failures_excluded  # printed, never decides
+  multiple_comparisons: none                 # expected false positives at 0.90 over 6 components printed
+  drift_guard: {cli_version: fixed_per_batch, model_ids: fixed_per_batch}   # DEC-0407
+  order: trial_major_seeded_shuffle_within_block
+  took_effect_per_trial: true                # a miss → infrastructure_error, arm paused until --clear-arm (DEC-0418)
+  predicates:                                # DEC-0416; d = arm − A1 point estimate, [lo, hi] its 90 % interval, c/w = cost/wall-clock Δ %
+    investigate: "any applicable primary has lo > 0"
+    keep: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03 and hi < 0"
+    inconclusive: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03, or the arm's excluded share > 0.25, or no valid pair"
+    remove: "else every applicable primary has d >= -0.03 and (c <= -15 or w <= -15)"
+    simplify: "else (every applicable primary within -0.03, cost similar)"
+  review_catch: {defect_counts_once_across_gates: true, false_positive_dedupe: cited_region, verdict_accurate_iff: "CHANGES_REQUIRED when the key holds a high or critical defect, APPROVED when none"}   # DEC-0420
+  inconclusive_extension_trials: 2
+  h1: "a1_full beats a0_bare on at least one primary with the interval excluding zero, else halt before promotion"
+  a4_sensitivity: "a4_no_gates worse than a1_full on hidden_test_pass_rate with the interval excluding zero, else harden tasks before acting on other arms"
+  decision_states: [investigate, keep, inconclusive, remove, simplify, not_run_cut, inconclusive_by_power]
+  mde_cut: 0.10   # sprint Task 3.4: an arm whose MDE at affordable trials exceeds this is pre-declared inconclusive_by_power and not run

         # Simple check: compare file count (full SHA verification would be more thorough)
         EXPECTED_COUNT=$(jq -r '.files | length' "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
-        ACTUAL_COUNT=$(find "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude" -type f ! -path "*/.git/*" ! -path "*/overrides/*" ! -path "*/checksums.json" | wc -l)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# validate-suite.sh — cycle-130 ablation task-suite validator (SDD §3.2, DEC-0424)
     4	#
     5	# Checks every task of the ablation-2.0 suite before it is frozen, run or graded.
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   validate-suite.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
     9	#
    10	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0); the
    11	#                     tasks are <root>/tasks/<id>/task.yaml
    12	#   --smoke           also validate <root>/smoke/<id>/task.yaml (never counted)
    13	#   --allow-partial   skip the four-by-four type count (Sprint 258 state)
    14	#   --suite-file F    suite yaml (default evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml): arm ids
    15	#                     for the leakage check, arms' task_types, suite_version
    16	#
    17	# Checks (each violation is one stdout line `<task-id>: <reason>`):
    18	#   1. schema: id (= directory name), schema_version 1, type (feature-build |
    19	#      bug-fix | refactor | review-catch), source {kind, date, fix_commit?,
    20	#      base_commit?, bead?, origin?}, post_cutoff (bool), fixture (dir under the
    21	#      root; null only for review-catch), criterion (agent-facing; no path, file
    22	#      name or test name), success_criterion, test_command (array; null only for
    23	#      review-catch), regression_command (array | null), reference_patch (hidden/…
    24	#      | null; required for bug-fix and feature-build), grader_protected (array of
    25	#      relative paths present in the fixture), structural_check (hidden/… | null;
    26	#      required for refactor), bounds {max_turns{}, timeout_min{}} (phase → positive
    27	#      int), review_catch (null, or {fixture, manifest, labels?} for review-catch,
    28	#      both present), suite_version (= the suite file's), TASK.md present
    29	#   2. counts: four tasks of each type under tasks/ (unless --allow-partial)
    30	#   3. allowlist: test_command[0] and regression_command[0] in python3 | pytest |
    31	#      bats | bash | node | npx
    32	#   4. hidden/manifest.json (build types): {"files": [{src, dest}]}; every src
    33	#      exists under hidden/; every dest is relative, inside the tree, no `..`
    34	#   5. fixture path rule (build types): check_fixture_path_rule from
    35	#      lib/sandbox-mount.sh — no .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/
    36	#      or .run/ at the fixture's top level; the reference patch touches none either
    37	#   6. leakage: TASK.md and criterion (the task-brief text is built from these)
    38	#      and every phase prompt under evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts/ contain none
    39	#      of: the string `hidden` (any case), a hidden test file's stem, a defect id
    40	#      of the review manifest, a `D[0-9]{2}-` key, an arm id of the suite file
    41	#   7. suite file: every non-absent arm's task_types are known (all | build |
    42	#      review-catch | feature-build | bug-fix | refactor)
    43	#
    44	# Exit: 0 valid; 1 violations (every one listed); 2 usage / unreadable input.
    45	# Tested by evals/tests/validate-suite.bats.
    46	# =============================================================================
    47	set -euo pipefail
    48	export LC_ALL=C
    49	
    50	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    51	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    52	ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
    53	SUITE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
    54	PROMPTS_DIR="${LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/phase-prompts}"
    55	SMOKE=false ALLOW_PARTIAL=false
    56	
    57	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,45p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    58	die() { echo "validate-suite: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    59	
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    63	    --smoke) SMOKE=true; shift ;;
    64	    --allow-partial) ALLOW_PARTIAL=true; shift ;;
    65	    --suite-file) SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    67	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    68	  esac
    69	done
    70	[[ -n "$ROOT" && -d "$ROOT" ]] || die "suite root not found: ${ROOT:-<empty>}"
    71	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"
    72	[[ -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || die "suite file not found: $SUITE_FILE"
    73	for tool in yq jq python3; do command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing tool: $tool"; done
    74	# eval.yml trust boundary: a literal in-tree path, no variable on the source line
    75	pushd "$SCRIPT_DIR" >/dev/null
    76	# shellcheck source=lib/sandbox-mount.sh
    77	source ./lib/sandbox-mount.sh
    78	popd >/dev/null
    79	
    80	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/validate-suite.XXXXXX")"
    81	trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
    82	yq -o=json '.' "$SUITE_FILE" > "$WORK/suite.json" 2>/dev/null || die "suite file is not valid YAML: $SUITE_FILE"
    83	
    84	# Collect task directories: tasks/* (counted) and smoke/* (with --smoke).
    85	: > "$WORK/tasks.tsv"
    86	for group in tasks smoke; do
    87	  [[ "$group" == "smoke" && "$SMOKE" != "true" ]] && continue
    88	  [[ -d "$ROOT/$group" ]] || continue
    89	  for d in "$ROOT/$group"/*/; do
    90	    [[ -d "$d" ]] || continue
    91	    d="${d%/}"
    92	    n="$(basename "$d")"
    93	    j="$WORK/$group.$n.json"
    94	    if [[ ! -f "$d/task.yaml" ]]; then
    95	      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "-" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"; continue
    96	    fi
    97	    if yq -o=json '.' "$d/task.yaml" > "$j" 2>/dev/null && jq -e 'type == "object"' "$j" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    98	      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "$j" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"
    99	    else
   100	      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "!" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"
   101	    fi
   102	  done
   103	done
   104	
   105	# Python does the schema, counts, allowlist, manifest, leakage and suite checks;
   106	# it prints violations, and `FIXTURE\t<id>\t<dir>` lines for the path rule below.
   107	python3 -I - "$WORK/tasks.tsv" "$WORK/suite.json" "$ROOT" "$REPO_ROOT" "$ALLOW_PARTIAL" "$PROMPTS_DIR" > "$WORK/out.txt" <<'PY' || { cat "$WORK/out.txt" >&2 2>/dev/null; die "validator crashed"; }
   108	import json, os, re, sys
   109	
   110	tasks_tsv, suite_json, root, repo, allow_partial, prompts_dir = sys.argv[1:7]
   111	allow_partial = allow_partial == "true"
   112	suite = json.load(open(suite_json))
   113	out = []
   114	def bad(tid, msg): out.append(f"{tid}: {msg}")
   115	
   116	TYPES = ["feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor", "review-catch"]
   117	BUILD = {"feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor"}
   118	ALLOW = {"python3", "pytest", "bats", "bash", "node", "npx"}
   119	KNOWN_TASK_TYPES = {"all", "build", "review-catch", "feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor"}
   120	MOUNT_OWNED = (".claude", "CLAUDE.md", ".loa.config.yaml", "grimoires", ".run")
   121	REQUIRED = ["id", "schema_version", "type", "source", "post_cutoff", "fixture", "criterion",
   122	            "success_criterion", "test_command", "regression_command", "reference_patch",
   123	            "grader_protected", "structural_check", "bounds", "review_catch", "suite_version"]
   124	
   125	arms = [a for a in (suite.get("arms") or []) if isinstance(a, dict)]
   126	arm_ids = sorted({a.get("id") for a in arms if isinstance(a.get("id"), str)})
   127	for a in arms:
   128	    if a.get("absent") is True:
   129	        continue
   130	    tt = a.get("task_types")
   131	    if not isinstance(tt, list) or not tt:
   132	        bad("suite", f"arm {a.get('id')} has no task_types list")
   133	        continue
   134	    for t in tt:
   135	        if t not in KNOWN_TASK_TYPES:
   136	            bad("suite", f"arm {a.get('id')} task_types names unknown type '{t}'")
   137	suite_version = suite.get("suite_version")
   138	
   139	def rel_ok(p):
   140	    return isinstance(p, str) and p and not p.startswith("/") and ".." not in p.split("/") and "\\" not in p
   141	
   142	def is_str_list(v):
   143	    return isinstance(v, list) and all(isinstance(x, str) and x for x in v)
   144	
   145	def read(p):
   146	    try:
   147	        return open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   148	    except OSError:
   149	        return None
   150	
   151	prompt_texts = []
   152	if os.path.isdir(prompts_dir):
   153	    for f in sorted(os.listdir(prompts_dir)):
   154	        if f.endswith(".md"):
   155	            prompt_texts.append((f"phase-prompts/{f}", read(os.path.join(prompts_dir, f)) or ""))
   156	
   157	def leak_scan(tid, label, text, stems, defect_ids):
   158	    low = text.lower()
   159	    if "hidden" in low:
   160	        bad(tid, f"leak: {label} contains the string 'hidden'")
   161	    for s in stems:
   162	        if s and re.search(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(s.lower()) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])", low):
   163	            bad(tid, f"leak: {label} names the grader file stem '{s}'")
   164	    for d in defect_ids:
   165	        if d in text:
   166	            bad(tid, f"leak: {label} names defect id '{d}'")
   167	    m = re.search(r"\bD[0-9]{2}-", text)
   168	    if m:
   169	        bad(tid, f"leak: {label} carries a defect key pattern '{m.group(0)}'")
   170	    for a in arm_ids:
   171	        if re.search(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(a) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])", text):
   172	            bad(tid, f"leak: {label} names arm id '{a}'")
   173	
   174	counts = {t: 0 for t in TYPES}
   175	seen = {}
   176	for line in open(tasks_tsv, encoding="utf-8"):
   177	    line = line.rstrip("\n")
   178	    if not line:
   179	        continue
   180	    group, name, tdir, jpath = line.split("\t")
   181	    tid = f"{group}/{name}"
   182	    if jpath == "-":
   183	        bad(tid, "no task.yaml"); continue

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
#
# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
#
#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
#
# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
#
#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
#
# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
#
# Options:
#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
#                the current directory)
#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
#   -h, --help   this text
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"

usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }

MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
ROOT=""
OUT=""
CHECK=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
    --root)
      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out)
      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
  esac
done

if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
fi
[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
#
# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
#
# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
#                      (a path component of that name)
#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
#                  other
#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
#
# Last line on stdout:
#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
#
# Usage:
#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
#
# Options:
#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
#                    current directory)
#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
#   -h, --help       this text
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
#      not JSON with a `files` object
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }

ROOT=""
MANIFEST=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root)
      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --manifest)
      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
  esac
done

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# freeze.sh — cycle-130 ablation suite freeze (SDD §5.13, DEC-0404, DEC-0414)
     4	#
     5	# Writes or verifies <root>/MANIFEST.sha256, the suite's frozen identity: one
     6	# "<sha256>  <relpath>" line per file under <root>/tasks/ (and <root>/smoke/
     7	# with --smoke), relpath relative to the root, LC_ALL=C sorted, sha256 (Python
     8	# hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code, eval.yml trust boundary).
     9	# validate-suite.sh runs first; an invalid suite is never frozen or accepted.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   freeze.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--check] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
    13	#
    14	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0)
    15	#   --smoke           cover smoke/ too (passed to the validator as well)
    16	#   --check           recompute and compare with MANIFEST.sha256; write nothing
    17	#   --allow-partial   passed to validate-suite.sh (fewer than four tasks per type)
    18	#   --suite-file F    passed to validate-suite.sh
    19	#
    20	# Output: `freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 (N files, sha256 <digest of the manifest>)`
    21	# or `freeze: OK — N files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 …)`; on drift every
    22	# changed / added / removed path on its own line.
    23	#
    24	# Exit: 0 written / matches; 1 drift, missing manifest under --check, or the
    25	#       validator found violations; 2 usage.
    26	# Tested by evals/tests/freeze.bats.
    27	# =============================================================================
    28	set -euo pipefail
    29	export LC_ALL=C
    30	
    31	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    32	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    33	
    34	ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
    35	CHECK=false SMOKE=false
    36	VARGS=()
    37	
    38	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,26p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    39	die() { echo "freeze: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    40	
    41	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    42	  case "$1" in
    43	    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    44	    --smoke) SMOKE=true; VARGS+=(--smoke); shift ;;
    45	    --check) CHECK=true; shift ;;
    46	    --allow-partial) VARGS+=(--allow-partial); shift ;;
    47	    --suite-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || die "--suite-file needs a path"; VARGS+=(--suite-file "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    48	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    49	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    50	  esac
    51	done
    52	[[ -n "$ROOT" && -d "$ROOT" ]] || die "suite root not found: ${ROOT:-<empty>}"
    53	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"
    54	MANIFEST="$ROOT/MANIFEST.sha256"
    55	
    56	vrc=0
    57	"$SCRIPT_DIR/validate-suite.sh" --root "$ROOT" ${VARGS[@]+"${VARGS[@]}"} || vrc=$?
    58	if [[ $vrc -eq 1 ]]; then echo "freeze: refused — the suite does not validate" >&2; exit 1; fi
    59	[[ $vrc -eq 0 ]] || die "validate-suite.sh failed (exit $vrc)"
    60	
    61	# compute_manifest <out> — the manifest body for the current tree.
    62	compute_manifest() {
    63	  local out="$1" list dirs=(tasks)
    64	  [[ "$SMOKE" == "true" ]] && dirs+=(smoke)
    65	  list="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze-list.XXXXXX")"
    66	  local d
    67	  for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
    68	    [[ -d "$ROOT/$d" ]] || continue
    69	    ( cd "$ROOT" && find "$d" -type f -print )
    70	  done | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list"
    71	  if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then rm -f "$list"; die "a path under the suite holds a backslash"; fi
    72	  python3 -I - "$ROOT" "$list" > "$out" <<'PY' || { rm -f "$list"; die "hashing failed"; }
    73	import hashlib, os, sys
    74	root, listing = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    75	for rel in open(listing, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines():
    76	    if not rel:
    77	        continue
    78	    h = hashlib.sha256()
    79	    with open(os.path.join(root, rel), "rb") as f:
    80	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
    81	            h.update(b)
    82	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + rel)
    83	PY
    84	  rm -f "$list"
    85	}
    86	digest_of() { python3 -I -c 'import hashlib, sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$1"; }
    87	
    88	TMP="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze.XXXXXX")"
    89	trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT
    90	compute_manifest "$TMP"
    91	n="$(grep -c . "$TMP" || true)"
    92	
    93	if [[ "$CHECK" == "true" ]]; then
    94	  [[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || { echo "freeze: no MANIFEST.sha256 in $ROOT (run freeze.sh first)" >&2; exit 1; }
    95	  if cmp -s "$TMP" "$MANIFEST"; then
    96	    echo "freeze: OK — $n files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 $(digest_of "$MANIFEST"))"
    97	    exit 0
    98	  fi
    99	  echo "freeze: DRIFT against $MANIFEST:"
   100	  python3 -I - "$MANIFEST" "$TMP" <<'PY'
   101	import sys
   102	def load(p):
   103	    m = {}
   104	    for line in open(p, encoding="utf-8"):
   105	        line = line.rstrip("\n")
   106	        if line:
   107	            h, _, rel = line.partition("  ")
   108	            m[rel] = h
   109	    return m
   110	old, new = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
   111	for rel in sorted(set(old) | set(new)):
   112	    if rel not in new:
   113	        print(f"  removed  {rel}")
   114	    elif rel not in old:
   115	        print(f"  added    {rel}")
   116	    elif old[rel] != new[rel]:
   117	        print(f"  changed  {rel}")
   118	PY
   119	  exit 1
   120	fi
   121	
   122	cp "$TMP" "$MANIFEST.tmp" && mv "$MANIFEST.tmp" "$MANIFEST"
   123	echo "freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 ($n files, sha256 $(digest_of "$MANIFEST"))"
   124	exit 0

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# execute-agent.sh — agent-execution step for Loa Eval Sandbox trials
     4	#
     5	# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9 / SDD §3.6). Fills the slot at the top of the
     6	# grading step in run-eval.sh: a task that declares `.agent.skill` runs the
     7	# headless Claude CLI inside the sandbox before its graders; every other task
     8	# takes the pre-existing path untouched.
     9	#
    10	# What it does, in order:
    11	#   1. Gate: no `.agent.skill` in the task YAML → exit 3, nothing written.
    12	#   2. Materialize the prompt surface from $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE into the sandbox:
    13	#        <ws>/.claude/skills/<skill>/        (SKILL.md + resources/)
    14	#        <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      (+ .claude/rules/)
    15	#        <ws>/CLAUDE.md                      → "@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    16	#        <ws>/.eval/skill-prompt.md          (SKILL.md body, frontmatter stripped)
    17	#      The prompt tree is the ONLY thing that differs between A/B arms, so it
    18	#      is recorded: prompt_tree_sha = `git rev-parse HEAD:.claude` of the tree,
    19	#      prompt_tree_commit, and whether .claude/ had uncommitted changes.
    20	#   3. Run:  claude -p "<task.prompt>" --output-format stream-json --verbose
    21	#              --model $EVAL_MODEL [--effort <e>] --restricted --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Write
    22	#              --permission-mode acceptEdits --append-system-prompt-file <skill-prompt>
    23	#              --max-turns $EVAL_MAX_TURNS
    24	#      --restricted --tools names the SDD's fixed tool set EXACTLY: it removes the
    25	#      code-running tools, ignores the operator's user/project/local settings (their
    26	#      Bash(...) allow rules leaked into the sprint-237 A/B arms under --allowed-tools,
    27	#      which only adds rules) and confines Read/Grep/Glob/Write to the sandbox.
    28	#      Edit/MultiEdit are therefore unavailable; the transcript extractor below still
    29	#      records them defensively.
    30	#      cwd = sandbox; env-isolated (LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH / LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH and
    31	#      TMPDIR into the sandbox; GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/OPENAI_API_KEY/AWS_* unset;
    32	#      HOME and PATH stay so the CLI finds its own credentials and toolchain).
    33	#   4. Record <ws>/.eval/events.jsonl (raw stream), agent-output.json (the
    34	#      `result` event) and executor.json:
    35	#        {schema_version, skill, model_requested, model_id (the id the CLI
    36	#         echoed — the modelUsage entry with the most output tokens), effort,
    37	#         prompt_tree_sha, prompt_tree_commit, prompt_tree_dirty, exit_code,
    38	#         is_error, duration_ms, num_turns, total_cost_usd, usage{…},
    39	#         tool_writes:[{seq,tool,path}] in transcript order}
    40	#
    41	# Exit codes:
    42	#   0  agent ran (its own verdict is the graders' business)
    43	#   1  the CLI exited non-zero or timed out (executor.json still written)
    44	#   2  infrastructure error (CLI binary missing, prompt tree lacks the skill)
    45	#   3  task declares no agent (caller should not have called us)
    46	#
    47	# Env:

    49	#   EVAL_EFFORT         override effort                    (default: task/skill)

# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
files=()

  case "$path" in
    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
  esac
  case "$path" in
    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
  esac
  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
    continue
  fi
  files+=("$path")
done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)

# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
: > "$TSV"
n=${#files[@]}
i=0
while [[ $i -lt $n ]]; do
  chunk=("${files[@]:i:400}")
  hashes=()
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    hashes+=("${line%% *}")
  done < <(cd "$ROOT" && sha256_portable "${chunk[@]}")
  [[ ${#hashes[@]} -eq ${#chunk[@]} ]] || die2 "sha256 returned ${#hashes[@]} digests for ${#chunk[@]} paths"
  j=0
  while [[ $j -lt ${#chunk[@]} ]]; do
    [[ "${hashes[j]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || die2 "unexpected sha256 output for ${chunk[j]}"
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "${chunk[j]}" "${hashes[j]}" >> "$TSV"
    j=$((j + 1))
  done
  i=$((i + 400))
done
[[ $n -gt 0 ]] || echo "gen-checksums: warning: no tracked files under .claude in $ROOT" >&2

GEN="${TMP_DIR}/checksums.json"
jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
  {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
   files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {key: .[0], value: .[1]}] | from_entries)}
' < "$TSV" > "$GEN"

# --- 3a. write ----------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ $CHECK -eq 0 ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
  chmod 0644 "$GEN"
  # mv replaces a symlinked manifest instead of writing through it.
  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
  exit 0
fi

# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]]; then
  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
  exit 1
fi
DIFF="${TMP_DIR}/diff.txt"
jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]
  + [ $o | keys[] | . as $p | select($n | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "removed"} ]
  + [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select(($o | has($p)) and $o[$p] != $n[$p]) | {p: $p, k: "changed"} ] )
  | sort_by(.p) | .[] | "\(.k): \(.p)"
' > "$DIFF"
count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')
if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "gen-checksums: --check: OK ($n entries match $OUT)" >&2
  exit 0
fi
echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2
sed -n '1,10s/^/  /p' "$DIFF" >&2
[[ "$count" -le 10 ]] || echo "  ... and $((count - 10)) more" >&2
echo "gen-checksums: regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
exit 1

4	#
5	# cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.6 (SDD D-4.5, DEC-0421, DEC-0423, DEC-0396).
6	# Extracted from execute-agent.sh (cycle-129 step 2 and the toggle functions)
7	# WITHOUT behaviour change for the cycle-129 single-skill path, and shared with
8	# pipeline-run.sh. Source it; it defines functions only and sets no shell
9	# options (the caller runs under `set -euo pipefail`).
10	#
11	# Contract (every function returns 0 on success, 2 when refused / when a step
12	# cannot take effect; refusals name the reason on one stderr line):
13	#
14	#   mount_prompt_surface <ws> <prompt_tree> <skill|->
15	#       skill given: <ws>/.claude/skills/<skill>/ (whole dir), .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md,
16	#       .claude/rules/, CLAUDE.md = "@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"; the prompt tree's
17	#       .loa.config.yaml only in arm mode (LOA_EVAL_ARM set), as cycle-129 did.
18	#       skill "-": the whole .claude/ tree is copied (files, never a symlink to the
19	#       tree), CLAUDE.md as above, and .loa.config.yaml always (the pipeline
20	#       executor needs every skill, hook and script). Evidence: mount=skill:<s>|tree.
21	#   resolve_arm_toggles <arm> <suite_file>
22	#       prints the arm's toggles as compact JSON on stdout. Arms are read from
23	#       `.arms[]` (ablation-2.0) and `.ab.arms[]` (recall suites). An arm with
24	#       toggles {} (a1_full, baseline) prints {}; `baseline` undeclared prints {}.
25	#       Exit 2: undeclared arm (an unreadable suite file declares none), `absent: true` arm.
26	#   apply_arm_toggles <ws> <toggles_json> <arm>
27	#       applies every toggle to the SANDBOX COPY and verifies it afterwards; exit 2
28	#       when one cannot take effect or is unknown. Toggles and values:
29	#         companion_voice: false  flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false
30	#         karpathy_block: false   '## Karpathy Principles' out of CLAUDE.loa.md (+ constraints.json rows)
31	#         rule_files: false       stash-safety.md, skill-invariants.md out of .claude/rules/
32	#         audit_delta_instruction: false  the delta paragraph out of auditing-security/SKILL.md
33	#         loa_mount: false        verifies no .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml in <ws>
34	#                                 (the caller skips mount_prompt_surface); evidence loa_mount=none
35	#         effort: low|medium|high|xhigh|max

37	#                                 <ws>/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; every `default_effort` key in
38	#                                 <ws>/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml set to the value and its
39	#                                 .checksum (bare sha256 hex) refreshed when present.
40	#                                 The caller passes `--effort <v>` on argv.
41	#         gates: false            flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.enabled=false;
42	#                                 LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false exported in the CALLING shell
43	#                                 and written to $ARM_ENV_FILE (KEY=VALUE lines) when that is set
44	#         flatline: false         flatline_protocol.enabled=false
45	#         sprint_plan: false, context_resets: false
46	#                                 phase-set edits owned by the pipeline executor; recorded as
47	#                                 evidence here (the single-skill executor refuses them itself)
48	#   regen_sandbox_manifest <ws>
49	#       writes <ws>/.claude/checksums.json {generated, algorithm: sha256, files} over
50	#       every regular file under <ws>/.claude except overrides/ and the manifest
51	#       itself (LC_ALL=C order, sha256). tools/gen-checksums.sh (in the
52	#       prompt tree, $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE) is used instead when it exists AND <ws> is a
53	#       git repository tracking .claude files (it lists `git ls-files`). No .claude/
54	#       (loa_mount: false) → manifest_sha256=none, exit 0. Prints manifest_sha256=<hex>.

74	#
75	# Hashing is Python hashlib (_sm_sha256), never .claude/ code: see _sm_sha256.
76	# Callers source this file by a literal relative path (no variable expansion
77	# on the source line), as eval.yml's trust-boundary scan requires.
78	#
79	# Evidence: every function reports `key=value` lines (one line, no newline in
80	# the value). When ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE is set they are appended to that file;
81	# else they go to the descriptor in SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD (default 1).
82	# resolve_arm_toggles prints JSON on stdout and no evidence.
83	#
84	# Tested by evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats (directly and through execute-agent.sh)
85	# and evals/tests/execute-agent.bats.

88	[[ "${_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED:-}" == "true" ]] && return 0
89	_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED=true

91	_SM_LIB_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
92	_SM_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$_SM_LIB_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
93	
94	_sm_err() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; }
95	
96	# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.
97	# Python hashlib, not compat-lib's sha256_portable: the eval workflow runs the
98	# harness as the trusted copy against a PR's .claude/, so no harness script
99	# sources .claude/ code (eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"); run-arms.sh
100	# hashes the corpus the same way.
101	_sm_sha256() {
102	  python3 -I -c '
103	import hashlib, sys
104	for p in sys.argv[1:]:
105	    h = hashlib.sha256()
106	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
107	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
108	            h.update(b)
109	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + p)' "$@"
110	}

112	# _sm_evidence <key> <value> — one key=value line to the evidence sink.
113	_sm_evidence() {
114	  local line="$1=${2//$'\n'/ }"
115	  if [[ -n "${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
116	    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
117	  else
118	    local fd="${SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD:-1}"
119	    [[ "$fd" =~ ^[0-9]$ ]] || fd=1
120	    printf '%s\n' "$line" >&"$fd"
121	  fi
122	}

125	mount_prompt_surface() {
126	  local ws="$1" tree="$2" skill="${3:-}"
127	  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
128	  [[ -d "$tree/.claude" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: prompt tree has no .claude/: $tree"; return 2; }
129	  if [[ "$skill" == "-" ]]; then
130	    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude"
131	    cp -a "$tree/.claude/." "$ws/.claude/" || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: copying .claude/ failed"; return 2; }
132	    printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
133	    if [[ -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"; fi
134	    _sm_evidence mount "tree"
135	    return 0
136	  fi
137	  case "$skill" in */*|.*|'') _sm_err "invalid skill name '$skill'"; return 2 ;; esac
138	  local skill_src="$tree/.claude/skills/$skill"
139	  [[ -f "$skill_src/SKILL.md" ]] || { _sm_err "prompt tree $tree has no .claude/skills/$skill/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
140	  mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/skills" "$ws/.claude/loa"
141	  # Whole skill dir (resources included) so guarded reads inside the skill resolve.
142	  local skill_dst="$ws/.claude/skills/$skill"
143	  mkdir -p "$skill_dst"
144	  cp -a "$skill_src/." "$skill_dst/"
145	  if [[ -f "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" ]]; then
146	    cp "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
147	  fi
148	  if [[ -d "$tree/.claude/rules" ]]; then
149	    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/rules"
150	    cp -a "$tree/.claude/rules/." "$ws/.claude/rules/"
151	  fi
152	  printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
153	  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" && -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
154	    cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"
155	  fi
156	  _sm_evidence mount "skill:$skill"
157	  return 0
158	}

161	resolve_arm_toggles() {
162	  local arm="$1" suite_file="${2:-}"
163	  [[ "$arm" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { _sm_err "invalid arm id '$arm'"; return 2; }
164	  local found=0 entry=""
165	  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
166	    # an unreadable suite file reads as "not declared" (cycle-129 behaviour: baseline still resolves to {})
167	    entry="$(ARM="$arm" yq -o=json -I=0 '[((.arms // [])[]), ((.ab.arms // [])[])] | map(select(.id == strenv(ARM))) | .[0] // null' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)" \
168	      || entry=""
169	    [[ -n "$entry" && "$entry" != "null" ]] && found=1
170	  fi
171	  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 ]]; then
172	    [[ "$arm" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }
173	    _sm_err "arm '$arm' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (arms[] / ab.arms[])"
174	    return 2
175	  fi
176	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$entry")" == "true" ]]; then
177	    _sm_err "arm '$arm' is declared absent in $suite_file (never run): $(jq -r '.evidence // "no evidence"' <<<"$entry")"
178	    return 2
179	  fi
180	  local t
181	  t="$(jq -c '.toggles // {}' <<<"$entry")"
182	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$t" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not an object in $suite_file"; return 2; }
183	  printf '%s' "$t"
184	}

186	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
187	# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
188	# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
189	_sm_drop_md_section() {
190	  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmpdir="$3" tmp
191	  tmp="$(mktemp "$tmpdir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
192	  awk -v h="$heading" '
193	    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
194	    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
195	    skip { n++; next }
196	    { print }
197	    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
198	  mv "$tmp" "$f"
199	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
200	}
201	
202	# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
203	# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
204	# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
205	_sm_drop_paragraph() {
206	  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
207	import re, sys
208	path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
209	text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
210	paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
211	for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
212	    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
213	        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
214	            removed = paras[i]
215	            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
216	            del paras[i:i + 2]
217	            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
218	            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
219	            sys.exit(0)
220	sys.exit(1)
221	PY
222	}
223	
224	# Strip every `effort:` line from the YAML frontmatter of file $1 (frontmatter
225	# = line 1 `---` up to the next `---`). Prints 1 when a line was removed, else 0.
226	_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort() {
227	  local f="$1" tmp
228	  tmp="$(mktemp "$f.XXXXXX")"
229	  awk '
230	    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; print; next }
231	    fm == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 2; print; next }
232	    fm == 1 && /^effort:/ { n++; next }
233	    { print }
234	    END { print (n > 0 ? 1 : 0) > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
235	  cat "$tmp" > "$f"; rm -f "$tmp"
236	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
237	}

239	# 0 when file $1's frontmatter still carries an `effort:` line.
240	_sm_frontmatter_has_effort() {
241	  awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && $0 == "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && /^effort:/ { found = 1; exit 0 } END { exit (found ? 0 : 1) }' "$1"
242	}

244	_sm_cfg_set_false() {  # _sm_cfg_set_false <cfg> <yq-path>... ; verifies each
245	  local cfg="$1"; shift
246	  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
247	  local p
248	  for p in "$@"; do
249	    P="$p" yq -i 'eval(strenv(P)) = false' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null || return 1
250	    [[ "$(P="$p" yq -r 'eval(strenv(P))' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] || return 1
251	  done
252	  return 0
253	}

255	apply_arm_toggles() {
256	  local ws="$1" toggles="${2:-}" arm="${3:-}"
257	  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_arm_toggles: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
258	  [[ -n "$toggles" ]] || toggles='{}'
259	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$toggles" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not a JSON object"; return 2; }
260	  local eval_dir="$ws/.eval"
261	  mkdir -p "$eval_dir"
262	  local key val
263	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
264	    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
265	    if [[ "$key" == "effort" ]]; then
266	      case "$val" in low|medium|high|xhigh|max) ;; *) _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle effort=$val (want low|medium|high|xhigh|max)"; return 2 ;; esac
267	    elif [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
268	      _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)"; return 2
269	    fi
270	    case "$key" in
271	      companion_voice)
272	        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice \
273	          || { _sm_err "companion_voice toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
274	        _sm_evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
275	        ;;
276	      karpathy_block)
277	        local k="$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
278	        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md"; return 2; }
279	        n="$(_sm_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles' "$eval_dir")"
280	        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
281	          _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed"; return 2
282	        fi
283	        local cj="$ws/.claude/data/constraints.json" cjn="none"
284	        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
285	          # audit r1 DISS-C-008: a failed rewrite is exit 2, not a silent pass; verify afterwards
286	          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" \
287	            || { rm -f "$cj.tmp"; _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json could not be rewritten"; return 2; }
288	          mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
289	          cjn="$(jq '[(.constraints // [])[] | select(tostring | test("karpathy"; "i"))] | length' "$cj" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
290	          [[ "$cjn" == "0" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json still carries Karpathy rows ($cjn)"; return 2; }
291	        fi
292	        _sm_evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md; constraints.json karpathy rows after: ${cjn}"
293	        ;;
294	      rule_files)
295	        local r gone=""
296	        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
297	          if [[ -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$ws/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
298	          [[ ! -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { _sm_err "rule_files toggle: $r still present"; return 2; }
299	        done
300	        _sm_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
301	        ;;
302	      audit_delta_instruction)
303	        local s="$ws/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
304	        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
305	        _sm_drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
306	          || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md"; return 2; }
307	        _sm_evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
308	        ;;
309	      loa_mount)
310	        local p left=""
311	        for p in .claude CLAUDE.md .loa.config.yaml; do
312	          if [[ -e "$ws/$p" || -L "$ws/$p" ]]; then left="$left $p"; fi
313	        done
314	        [[ -z "$left" ]] || { _sm_err "loa_mount toggle: the sandbox still holds:$left (mount_prompt_surface must be skipped)"; return 2; }
315	        _sm_evidence loa_mount "none"
316	        ;;
317	      effort)
318	        local f total=0 stripped=0 still=""
319	        for f in "$ws"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
320	          [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
321	          total=$((total + 1))
322	          if [[ "$(_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort "$f")" == "1" ]]; then stripped=$((stripped + 1)); fi
323	          if _sm_frontmatter_has_effort "$f"; then still="$still ${f#"$ws"/}"; fi
324	        done
325	        [[ -z "$still" ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: effort: still in the frontmatter of:$still"; return 2; }
326	        local mc="$ws/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" cat_state="absent"
327	        if [[ -f "$mc" ]]; then
328	          local nkeys
329	          nkeys="$(yq '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort"))] | length' "$mc" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
330	          [[ "$nkeys" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$nkeys" -gt 0 ]] \

376	regen_sandbox_manifest() {
377	  local ws="$1"
378	  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
379	  if [[ ! -d "$ws/.claude" ]]; then

382	  fi
383	  local out="$ws/.claude/checksums.json" tool="${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}/tools/gen-checksums.sh" how="inline"
384	  if [[ -x "$tool" ]] && git -C "$ws" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 \
385	     && [[ -n "$(git -C "$ws" ls-files .claude 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]]; then
386	    "$tool" --root "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: $tool --root $ws failed"; return 2; }
387	    how="gen-checksums.sh"
388	  else

390	    mkdir -p "$ws/.eval"
391	    ( cd "$ws" && find .claude -type f ! -path '.claude/overrides/*' ! -path '.claude/checksums.json' -print ) \
392	      | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list"
393	    if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: a path under .claude/ holds a backslash"; rm -f "$list"; return 2; fi
394	    : > "$sums"
395	    local -a batch=()
396	    local f
397	    while IFS= read -r f; do
398	      batch+=("$f")
399	      if [[ ${#batch[@]} -ge 200 ]]; then
400	        ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; }
401	        batch=()
402	      fi

404	    if [[ ${#batch[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
405	      ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; }
406	    fi

408	      {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
409	       files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | capture("^(?<h>[0-9a-f]{64})  (?<p>.+)$") | {key: .p, value: .h}] | from_entries)}' \
410	      < "$sums" > "$out.tmp" || { rm -f "$out.tmp" "$list" "$sums"; _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: could not write the manifest"; return 2; }
411	    mv "$out.tmp" "$out"
412	    rm -f "$list" "$sums"
413	  fi
414	  jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: $out is not a manifest"; return 2; }
415	  local digest
416	  digest="$(_sm_sha256 "$out" | awk '{print $1}')"
417	  _sm_evidence manifest_files "$(jq '.files | length' "$out") ($how)"
418	  _sm_evidence manifest_sha256 "$digest"
419	  return 0
