1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
     6	# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
     7	# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
     8	# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
     9	# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
    10	#
    11	# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
    12	#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
    13	#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
    14	#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
    15	#                      (a path component of that name)
    16	#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
    17	#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
    18	#                  other
    19	#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
    20	# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
    21	# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
    22	#
    23	# Last line on stdout:
    24	#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
    28	#
    29	# Options:
    30	#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
    31	#                    current directory)
    32	#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
    33	#   -h, --help       this text
    34	#
    35	# Exit codes:
    36	#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
    37	#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
    38	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
    39	#      not JSON with a `files` object
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	
    47	ROOT=""
    48	MANIFEST=""
    49	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    50	  case "$1" in
    51	    --root)
    52	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    53	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    54	    --manifest)
    55	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
    56	      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    57	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    58	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    59	  esac
    60	done
    61	
    62	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    63	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    64	fi
    65	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    66	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    67	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    68	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    69	[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
    70	[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
    71	jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    72	  || die2 "manifest is not JSON with a files object: $MANIFEST"
    73	
    74	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
    75	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    76	trap cleanup EXIT
    77	
    78	# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
    79	# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
    80	git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
    81	jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
    82	comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
    83	comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
    84	
    85	classify() {
    86	  local p="$1"
    87	  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
    88	    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    89	  elif [[ "$p" == *.pyc ]]; then
    90	    printf '.pyc'
    91	  elif [[ "$p" == *.lock ]]; then
    92	    printf '.lock'
    93	  else
    94	    printf 'other'
    95	  fi
    96	}
    97	
    98	# Classified untracked offenders: "<class>\t<path>"
    99	: > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   100	while IFS= read -r p; do
   101	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   102	  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(classify "$p")" "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   103	done < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
   104	
   105	: > "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   106	while IFS= read -r p; do
   107	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   108	  [[ -e "${ROOT}/${p}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   109	done < "${TMP_DIR}/both"
   110	
   111	entries=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/listed" | tr -d ' ')
   112	n_untracked=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | tr -d ' ')
   113	n_missing=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/missing" | tr -d ' ')
   114	
   115	class_summary=""
   116	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 ]]; then
   117	  echo "check-manifest-paths: untracked manifest paths (not in git ls-files -- .claude), by class:" >&2
   118	  for cls in __pycache__ .pytest_cache node_modules .run .pyc .lock other; do
   119	    c=$(awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
   120	    [[ "$c" -gt 0 ]] || continue
   121	    class_summary="${class_summary:+${class_summary}, }${cls}=${c}"
   122	    echo "  [${cls}] ${c} path(s):" >&2
   123	    awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c { print "    " $2 }' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" >&2
   124	  done
   125	fi
   126	if [[ "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   127	  echo "check-manifest-paths: tracked manifest paths absent from the working tree:" >&2
   128	  sed 's/^/    /' "${TMP_DIR}/missing" >&2
   129	fi
   130	
   131	echo "manifest-paths: ${entries} entries, ${n_untracked} untracked${class_summary:+ (${class_summary})}, ${n_missing} missing"
   132	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 || "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   133	  echo "check-manifest-paths: FAIL — regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   134	  exit 1
   135	fi
   136	exit 0

96	    96	# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.
97	    97	# Python hashlib, not compat-lib's sha256_portable: the eval workflow runs the
98	    98	# harness as the trusted copy against a PR's .claude/, so no harness script
99	    99	# sources .claude/ code (eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"); run-arms.sh
100	   100	# hashes the corpus the same way.
101	   101	_sm_sha256() {
102	   102	  python3 -I -c '
103	   103	import hashlib, sys
104	   104	for p in sys.argv[1:]:
105	   105	    h = hashlib.sha256()
106	   106	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
107	   107	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
108	   108	            h.update(b)
109	   109	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + p)' "$@"
110	   110	}

187	   187	# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
188	   188	# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
189	   189	_sm_drop_md_section() {
190	   190	  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmpdir="$3" tmp
191	   191	  tmp="$(mktemp "$tmpdir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
192	   192	  awk -v h="$heading" '
193	   193	    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
194	   194	    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
195	   195	    skip { n++; next }
196	   196	    { print }
197	   197	    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"

202	   202	# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
203	   203	# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
204	   204	# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
205	   205	_sm_drop_paragraph() {
206	   206	  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
207	   207	import re, sys
208	   208	path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
209	   209	text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
210	   210	paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
211	   211	for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
212	   212	    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
213	   213	        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
214	   214	            removed = paras[i]
215	   215	            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
216	   216	            del paras[i:i + 2]
217	   217	            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
218	   218	            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
219	   219	            sys.exit(0)
220	   220	sys.exit(1)
221	   221	PY
222	   222	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
     6	# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
     7	# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
     8	# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
     9	# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
    10	# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
    11	#
    12	#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
    13	#
    14	# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
    15	# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
    16	# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
    17	#
    18	#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
    19	#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
    20	#
    21	# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
    22	# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
    23	# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
    24	# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
    28	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
    32	#                the current directory)
    33	#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
    34	#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
    35	#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
    36	#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
    37	#   -h, --help   this text
    38	#
    39	# Exit codes:
    40	#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
    41	#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
    42	#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
    43	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
    44	#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
    45	# =============================================================================
    46	set -euo pipefail
    47	export LC_ALL=C
    48	
    49	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    50	# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
    51	source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    52	
    53	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    54	die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    55	
    56	MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
    57	ROOT=""
    58	OUT=""
    59	CHECK=0
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
    63	    --root)
    64	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    65	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --out)
    67	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
    68	      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    69	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    70	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    71	  esac
    72	done

+# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and

+# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.

+# Usage:
+#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
+#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
+#                the current directory)
+#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
+#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
+#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
+#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written

+#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
+#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
+#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that

+  done

+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
+  chmod 0644 "$GEN"

+  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
+  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
+  exit 0
+fi

+# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------

+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi

+jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
+  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
+  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]

+count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')

+  exit 0
+fi
+echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
     4	#
     5	# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
     6	# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
     7	# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
     8	#
     9	# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
    10	#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
    11	#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
    12	#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
    13	#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
    14	#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
    15	#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
    16	#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
    17	#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
    18	#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
    19	#                    submodule from there; no network).
    20	#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
    21	#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
    22	#      is printed, then a summary line
    23	#        fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=T Missing=M not-mounted=N check-loa-rc=R
    24	#
    25	# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
    26	# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
    27	# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
    28	#
    29	# Usage:
    30	#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]
    31	#
    32	# Options:
    33	#   --ref REF    commit-ish of this repository to mount (default: HEAD of the
    34	#                repository the script lives in)
    35	#   --worktree   mount REF plus the source work tree's uncommitted state
    36	#                (use before the change is committed)
    37	#   --keep       keep the temp directory and print its path
    38	#   --tmp DIR    parent directory for the temp directory (default: $TMPDIR or
    39	#                /tmp)
    40	#   -h, --help   this text
    41	#
    42	# Exit codes:
    43	#   0    check-loa.sh exited 0 on the fresh mount
    44	#   1    check-loa.sh exited non-zero (its output names the failures)
    45	#   2    usage error
    46	#   3    setup failed (clone, overlay, downstream init or the mount itself);
    47	#        the failing step's output is printed
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    53	die2() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	die3() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: SETUP FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 3; }
    55	
    56	REF=""
    57	KEEP=0
    58	WORKTREE=0
    59	TMP_PARENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --ref)
    63	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--ref requires a commit-ish"
    64	      REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    65	    --tmp)
    66	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--tmp requires a directory"
    67	      TMP_PARENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    68	    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    69	    --worktree) WORKTREE=1; shift ;;
    70	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    71	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    72	  esac
    73	done
    74	[[ -d "$TMP_PARENT" ]] || die2 "--tmp is not a directory: $TMP_PARENT"
    75	
    76	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
    77	SRC="$(git -C "$SELF_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "script is not inside a git work tree"
    78	[[ -n "$REF" ]] || REF="HEAD"
    79	REF_SHA="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${REF}^{commit}")" || die2 "not a commit in $SRC: $REF"
    80	
    81	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMP_PARENT%/}/fresh-mount-proof.XXXXXX")"
    82	cleanup() {
    83	  if [[ $KEEP -eq 1 ]]; then
    84	    echo "fresh-mount-proof: kept $WORK" >&2
    85	  else
    86	    rm -rf "$WORK"
    87	  fi
    88	}
    89	trap cleanup EXIT
    90	
    91	# --- hermetic git ---------------------------------------------------------------
    92	mkdir -p "$WORK/no-hooks"
    93	export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
    94	export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3
    95	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=always
    96	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="$WORK/no-hooks"
    97	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=init.defaultBranch GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=main
    98	export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="fresh-mount-proof" GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="fresh-mount-proof@localhost"
    99	export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"
   100	unset LOA_ALEPH_ENABLED
   101	
   102	LOG="$WORK/step.log"
   103	run_step() {  # run_step <description> <cmd...>; output to $LOG, printed on failure
   104	  local desc="$1"; shift
   105	  if ! "$@" > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
   106	    cat "$LOG" >&2
   107	    die3 "$desc"
   108	  fi
   109	}
   110	
   111	suffix=""
   112	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && suffix=" + work-tree state"
   113	echo "fresh-mount-proof: source $SRC at ${REF_SHA}${suffix}"
   114	echo "fresh-mount-proof: temp dir $WORK"
   115	
   116	# --- 1. upstream clone ----------------------------------------------------------
   117	UP="$WORK/upstream"
   118	run_step "clone $SRC" git clone --quiet --no-checkout "file://$SRC" "$UP"
   119	run_step "fetch $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" fetch --quiet origin "$REF_SHA"
   120	run_step "branch at $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" checkout --quiet -B fresh-mount-proof "$REF_SHA"
   121	
   122	overlay() {
   123	  local p
   124	  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
   125	    if [[ -e "$SRC/$p" || -L "$SRC/$p" ]]; then
   126	      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
   127	      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"
   128	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   129	      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
   130	    else
   131	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   132	    fi
   133	  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)
   134	  git -C "$UP" add -A
   135	  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"
   136	}
   137	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && run_step "work-tree overlay" overlay
   138	MOUNT_SHA="$(git -C "$UP" rev-parse HEAD)"
   139	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mounting upstream commit $MOUNT_SHA"
   140	
   141	# --- 2. downstream repository and the submodule mount --------------------------
   142	DOWN="$WORK/downstream"
   143	mkdir -p "$DOWN"
   144	init_downstream() {
   145	  git -C "$DOWN" init --quiet
   146	  printf '# downstream fixture\n' > "$DOWN/README.md"
   147	  git -C "$DOWN" add README.md
   148	  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"
   149	}
   150	run_step "downstream init" init_downstream
   151	
   152	do_mount() {
   153	  (cd "$DOWN" && LOA_UPSTREAM="file://$UP" bash "$UP/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh" \
   154	    --branch fresh-mount-proof --ref "$MOUNT_SHA" --force < /dev/null)
   155	}
   156	run_step "mount-submodule.sh" do_mount
   157	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mount-submodule.sh exited 0 ($(grep -c 'Linked' "$LOG" || true) link lines)"
   158	
   159	# --- 3. Aleph off ---------------------------------------------------------------
   160	CFG="$DOWN/.loa.config.yaml"
   161	[[ -f "$CFG" ]] || : > "$CFG"
   162	if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   163	  run_step "aleph.enabled: false" yq -i '.aleph.enabled = false' "$CFG"
   164	else
   165	  printf '\naleph:\n  enabled: false\n' >> "$CFG"
   166	fi
   167	
   168	# --- 4. check-loa.sh ------------------------------------------------------------
   169	OUT="$WORK/check-loa.out"
   170	rc=0
   171	(cd "$DOWN" && CI=true bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh < /dev/null) > "$OUT" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   172	echo "----- check-loa.sh (downstream) -----"
   173	cat "$OUT"
   174	echo "----- end check-loa.sh (exit $rc) -----"
   175	
   176	tampered=$(grep -c 'Tampered: ' "$OUT" || true)
   177	missing=$(grep -c 'Missing: ' "$OUT" || true)
   178	not_mounted=$(sed -n 's/.*not-mounted: \([0-9][0-9]*\) path(s).*/\1/p' "$OUT")
   179	echo "fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=${tampered} Missing=${missing} not-mounted=${not_mounted:-0} check-loa-rc=${rc}"
   180	[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && exit 0
   181	exit 1

printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$WORKSPACE/CLAUDE.md"

# --- 2b. control arm (cycle-129 FR-2) -----------------------------------------
ARM_MODE=false
[[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" ]] && ARM_MODE=true
ARM="${LOA_EVAL_ARM:-baseline}"
[[ "$ARM" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { echo "ERROR: invalid LOA_EVAL_ARM '$ARM'" >&2; exit 2; }
if [[ "$ARM_MODE" == "true" && -f "$PROMPT_TREE/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
  cp "$PROMPT_TREE/.loa.config.yaml" "$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
fi

# The arm's toggles: explicit JSON, else the suite's ab.arms[] entry.
resolve_toggles() {
  # audit r1 DISS-C-001: toggles exist only in arm mode (LOA_EVAL_ARM set); a stale
  # LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES in a non-arm environment is ignored, and the baseline arm
  # never carries toggles.
  if [[ "$ARM_MODE" != "true" ]]; then
    [[ -z "${LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES:-}" ]] || echo "WARN: LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES is set but LOA_EVAL_ARM is not: ignored (not an arm run)" >&2
    printf '{}'; return 0
  fi
  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES:-}" ]]; then
    jq -ce 'if type == "object" then . else error("not an object") end' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES" 2>/dev/null \
      || { echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES is not a JSON object" >&2; return 2; }
    if [[ "$ARM" == "baseline" && "$(jq -c 'length' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES")" != "0" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: the baseline arm takes no toggles (LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES=$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES)" >&2; return 2
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  local suite_file="${LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE:-}"
  if [[ -z "$suite_file" ]]; then
    local tdir; tdir="$(basename "$(dirname "$TASK_YAML")")"
    [[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml" ]] && suite_file="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml"
  fi
  local t="" found=0
  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
    found="$(ARM="$ARM" yq '[.ab.arms[]? | select(.id == strenv(ARM))] | length' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [[ "$found" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || found=0
    if [[ "$found" -gt 0 ]]; then
      t="$(ARM="$ARM" yq -o=json -I=0 '[.ab.arms[] | select(.id == strenv(ARM))][0].toggles // {}' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)"
    fi
  fi
  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 || -z "$t" || "$t" == "null" ]]; then
    [[ "$ARM" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }
    echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (ab.arms[])" >&2
    return 2
  fi
  printf '%s' "$t"
}
ARM_TOGGLES="$(resolve_toggles)" || exit 2

# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
_drop_md_section() {
  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp "$eval_dir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
  awk -v h="$heading" '
    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
    skip { n++; next }
    { print }
    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
  mv "$tmp" "$f"
  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
}

# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
_drop_paragraph() {
  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
import re, sys
path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
            removed = paras[i]
            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
            del paras[i:i + 2]
            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
            sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)
PY
}

ARM_EVIDENCE='{}'
_evidence() { ARM_EVIDENCE="$(jq -c --arg k "$1" --arg v "$2" '. + {($k): $v}' <<<"$ARM_EVIDENCE")"; }

apply_toggles() {
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json" cjn="none"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
          # audit r1 DISS-C-008: a failed rewrite is exit 2, not a silent pass; verify afterwards
          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" \
            || { rm -f "$cj.tmp"; echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json could not be rewritten" >&2; return 2; }
          mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
          cjn="$(jq '[(.constraints // [])[] | select(tostring | test("karpathy"; "i"))] | length' "$cj" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
          [[ "$cjn" == "0" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json still carries Karpathy rows ($cjn)" >&2; return 2; }
        fi
        _evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md; constraints.json karpathy rows after: ${cjn}"
        ;;
      rule_files)
        local r gone=""
        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
          if [[ -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
          [[ ! -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: $r still present" >&2; return 2; }
        done
        _evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
        ;;
      audit_delta_instruction)
        local s="$WORKSPACE/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
        _drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
          || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
        ;;
      *) echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' declares unknown toggle '$key'" >&2; return 2 ;;
    esac
  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$ARM_TOGGLES")
  return 0
}
apply_toggles || exit 2

# Skill body without the YAML frontmatter → the appended system prompt. Read
# from the (toggled) sandbox copy so an arm reaches the system prompt too.
awk 'BEGIN{fm=0} NR==1 && $0=="---"{fm=1; next} fm==1 && $0=="---"{fm=2; next} fm!=1{print}' \
  "$skill_dst/SKILL.md" > "$eval_dir/skill-prompt.md"

# Prompt-tree identity (what the A/B is actually varying).
prompt_tree_sha="$(git -C "$PROMPT_TREE" rev-parse HEAD:.claude 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
prompt_tree_commit="$(git -C "$PROMPT_TREE" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
# audit r1 DISS-C-009: a declared source commit is a hex id and, when the prompt tree's
# HEAD is known, the same commit — otherwise two trials from different trees could
# present one source_commit and pass compare.sh's skew check.
if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT:-}" ]]; then
  [[ "$LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ ]] \
    || { echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT is not a hex commit id" >&2; exit 2; }
  if [[ "$prompt_tree_commit" != "unknown" && "$prompt_tree_commit" != "$LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT"* ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT ($LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT) is not the prompt tree's HEAD ($prompt_tree_commit)" >&2; exit 2
  fi
fi
prompt_tree_dirty=false
if [[ -n "$(git -C "$PROMPT_TREE" status --porcelain -- .claude 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
  prompt_tree_dirty=true
fi

# Effort: env > task > skill frontmatter > none; invalid → none.
resolve_effort() {
  local cand="${EVAL_EFFORT:-}"
  if [[ -z "$cand" ]]; then
    cand="$(yq -r '.agent.effort // ""' "$TASK_YAML")"
  fi
  if [[ -z "$cand" || "$cand" == "null" ]]; then
    cand="$(awk 'NR==1 && $0!="---"{exit} NR>1 && $0=="---"{exit} NR>1{print}' "$skill_src/SKILL.md" \
      | yq -r '.effort // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi
  case "$cand" in
    low|medium|high|xhigh|max) printf '%s' "$cand" ;;
    *) printf '' ;;
  esac
}
effort="$(resolve_effort)"

prompt="$(yq -r '.prompt // ""' "$TASK_YAML")"
[[ -n "$prompt" && "$prompt" != "null" ]] || { echo "ERROR: task has no prompt" >&2; exit 2; }

# --- 3. run ------------------------------------------------------------------
argv=(
  "$CLAUDE_BIN" -p "$prompt"
  --output-format stream-json --verbose
  --model "$MODEL"
  --restricted --tools "Read,Grep,Glob,Write"
  --permission-mode acceptEdits
  --append-system-prompt-file "$eval_dir/skill-prompt.md"
  --max-turns "$MAX_TURNS"
)
[[ -n "$effort" ]] && argv+=(--effort "$effort")

events="$eval_dir/events.jsonl"
stderr_log="$eval_dir/agent-stderr.log"
start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
rc=0
(
  cd "$WORKSPACE" || exit 2
  export LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH="$eval_dir/model-invoke.jsonl"
  export LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH="$eval_dir/cost-ledger.jsonl"
  export EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL"
  # sprint-237 audit HIGH-001: the CLI keeps HOME (its own credentials live there)
  # and PATH (its toolchain); the operator's other credentials are not the agent
  # under test's business, and its temp files stay inside the sandbox.
  unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN OPENAI_API_KEY AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
  # cycle-129: an executor started from inside a Claude Code session inherits
  # that session's coupling (child-session flag, session id, messaging socket,
  # agent teams) and its subagent model (the sprint-255 driver session carried
  # CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=opus). Decouple the session and pin every
  # auxiliary model to the executor model. (A safeguard-refusal fallback to
  # another model is a separate CLI behaviour, recorded below as
  # refusal_fallbacks; no environment setting turns it off.)
  unset CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET \
    CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED
  export CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL="$MODEL"
  mkdir -p "$eval_dir/tmp" && export TMPDIR="$eval_dir/tmp"
  exec timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15 "$TIMEOUT_S" "${argv[@]}"
) > "$events" 2> "$stderr_log" || rc=$?
end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
duration_ms=$(( end_ms - start_ms ))

# --- 4. record ---------------------------------------------------------------
# The last `result` event is the CLI's summary (absent on crash/timeout).
result_json="$(grep -E '^\{.*"type" *: *"result"' "$events" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)"
if [[ -z "$result_json" ]] || ! jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$result_json"; then
  result_json='{"type":"result","subtype":"missing","is_error":true}'
fi
printf '%s\n' "$result_json" > "$eval_dir/agent-output.json"

# Ordered tool writes from the transcript (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit).
tool_writes="$(jq -c '
  select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]? |
  select(.type=="tool_use" and (.name=="Write" or .name=="Edit" or .name=="MultiEdit" or .name=="NotebookEdit")) |
  {tool:.name, path:(.input.file_path // .input.notebook_path // "")}
' "$events" 2>/dev/null | jq -sc 'to_entries | map({seq:(.key+1), tool:.value.tool, path:.value.path})' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"
[[ -n "$tool_writes" ]] || tool_writes='[]'

# cycle-129: a safeguard refusal makes the CLI retry the session on another
# model (system/model_refusal_fallback); the arm run must see it, because the
# output after it is not the requested executor's.
refusal_fallbacks="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="system" and .subtype=="model_refusal_fallback")
  | {from: (.original_model // null), to: (.fallback_model // null), category: (.api_refusal_category // null),
     scope: (.scope // null)}' "$events" 2>/dev/null | jq -sc '.' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"
[[ -n "$refusal_fallbacks" ]] || refusal_fallbacks='[]'

is_error="$(jq -r '.is_error // false' <<<"$result_json")"
[[ $rc -ne 0 ]] && is_error=true

jq -n \
  --arg skill "$skill" \
  --arg model_requested "$MODEL" \
  --arg effort "$effort" \
  --arg prompt_tree "$PROMPT_TREE" \
  --arg prompt_tree_sha "$prompt_tree_sha" \
  --arg prompt_tree_commit "$prompt_tree_commit" \
  --argjson prompt_tree_dirty "$prompt_tree_dirty" \
  --arg run_id "$RUN_ID" \
  --arg trial_id "$TRIAL_ID" \
  --argjson rc "$rc" \
  --argjson is_error "$is_error" \
  --argjson duration_ms "$duration_ms" \
  --argjson result "$result_json" \
  --argjson tool_writes "$tool_writes" \
  --arg arm "$ARM" \
  --argjson arm_toggles "$ARM_TOGGLES" \
  --argjson arm_evidence "$ARM_EVIDENCE" \
  --arg source_commit "${LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT:-$prompt_tree_commit}" \
  --argjson refusal_fallbacks "$refusal_fallbacks" \
  '
  def norm_usage(u): {
    input_tokens: (u.input_tokens // u.inputTokens // 0),
    output_tokens: (u.output_tokens // u.outputTokens // 0),
    cache_creation_input_tokens: (u.cache_creation_input_tokens // u.cacheCreationInputTokens // 0),
    cache_read_input_tokens: (u.cache_read_input_tokens // u.cacheReadInputTokens // 0)
  };
  ($result.modelUsage // {}) as $mu |
  # the model that produced the output: the modelUsage entry with the most
  # output tokens (a haiku helper call must not be mis-attributed — the
  # framework-review 2026-09-17 rec 5 class), else the requested id.
  (if ($mu | length) > 0
     then ($mu | to_entries | max_by(.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0) | .key)
     else $model_requested end) as $model_id |
  {
    schema_version: 1,
    skill: $skill,
    run_id: $run_id,
    trial_id: $trial_id,
    model_requested: $model_requested,
    model_id: $model_id,
    effort: $effort,
    prompt_tree: $prompt_tree,
    prompt_tree_sha: $prompt_tree_sha,
    prompt_tree_commit: $prompt_tree_commit,
    prompt_tree_dirty: $prompt_tree_dirty,
    exit_code: $rc,
    is_error: $is_error,
    duration_ms: $duration_ms,
    num_turns: ($result.num_turns // 0),
    total_cost_usd: ($result.total_cost_usd // 0),
    usage: norm_usage($result.usage // {}),
    models_used: ($mu | with_entries(.value = (.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0))),
    refusal_fallbacks: $refusal_fallbacks,
    tool_writes: $tool_writes,
    arm: $arm,
    arm_toggles: $arm_toggles,
    arm_evidence: $arm_evidence,
    source_commit: $source_commit
  }' > "$eval_dir/executor.json"

if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo "execute-agent: CLI exited $rc (see $stderr_log)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

     4	# (cycle-130 FR-3/FR-7, SDD §1.4 D-4.2, §5.10; DEC-0418)
     5	#
     6	# Evaluates the rule ids the suite file lists under the arm's `took_effect` against
     7	# one run directory written by pipeline-run.sh (or every run under --batch-dir).
     8	# Evidence is read from what the run produced — meta/pipeline.json, the
     9	# meta/phase-<label>.argv.json captures (argv + environment), eval/model-invoke.jsonl,
    10	# the dissent envelopes and the sandbox tree — never from what the agent said.
    11	#
    12	# Rules:
    13	#   no_dot_claude              sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md
    14	#   no_system_prompt           no argv carries --append-system-prompt-file
    15	#   no_audit_rows              no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl (no hook ran)
    16	#   all_phases_present         the phase records equal the arm's phase set for the task
    17	#                              type (skipped FIX rounds count as records); a run that
    18	#                              stopped early (cap_failure, agent_error, interrupted)
    19	#                              passes when its records are a prefix of the set
    20	#   no_plan_phase              no PLAN record
    21	#   one_voice_planned          both envelopes (review, audit) say companion_voice.planned false
    22	#   no_gate_phases             no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record
    23	#   enforce_env_false          every captured phase env has LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false
    24	#   no_flatline_rows           no eval/ MODELINV row whose calling_primitive starts with
    25	#                              flatline, and sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md exists
    26	#   implementer_single_session one non-null session_id across the executed PLAN, IMPLEMENT
    27	#                              and FIX records, and every continuation's argv resumes it
    28	#   gates_separate_sessions    REVIEW and AUDIT session ids are non-null, distinct from
    29	#                              each other and from every implementer session id
    30	#   effort_flag_medium         every argv carries --effort medium
    31	#   skill_effort_stripped      no sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter has an ^effort:
    32	#                              line (the block between the first two `---` lines; body lines
    33	#                              are not frontmatter)
    34	#   integrity_clean            arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 is present and every entry of
    35	#                              sandbox/.claude/checksums.json hashes to its recorded value
    36	#                              (Python hashlib walk); a loa_mount: false arm passes with
    37	#                              "no mount"
    38	#   applicability_refused      a refusal record (meta/refused.json) names this arm and a task
    39	#                              type outside its task_types; a run that was not refused passes
    40	#                              when its task type is inside task_types (and fails otherwise)
    41	# A refusal record is evaluated on applicability_refused alone.
    42	#
    43	# Usage:
    44	#   took-effect.sh --run-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
    45	#   took-effect.sh --batch-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
    46	#
    47	# Output: `arm <id>: <rule> OK|FAIL <evidence>` per rule, then `arm <id>: OK` or
    48	# `arm <id>: FAIL (<n> of <m> rules)`; --batch-dir adds `took-effect: <runs> runs, <k> failed`.
    49	# --json prints one object per run ({run_dir, arm, ok, rules: [{rule, ok, evidence}]}).
    50	#
    51	# Exit codes:
    52	#   0  every rule OK
    53	#   1  any rule FAIL
    54	#   2  usage error (missing files, unknown arm)
    55	#
    56	# Tested by evals/tests/took-effect.bats (fixture runs under
    57	# evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/).
    58	# =============================================================================
    59	set -euo pipefail
    60	export LC_ALL=C
    61	
    62	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
    63	# "Validate grader trust boundary").
    64	
    65	RUN_DIR="" BATCH_DIR="" SUITE_FILE="" ARM_OPT="" JSON=false
    66	usage() { echo "took-effect.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    67	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    68	  case "$1" in
    69	    --run-dir)    RUN_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    70	    --batch-dir)  BATCH_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    71	    --suite-file) SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    72	    --arm)        ARM_OPT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    73	    --json)       JSON=true; shift ;;
    74	    -h|--help)    sed -n '2,56p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    75	    *) usage "unknown argument: $1" ;;
    76	  esac
    77	done
    78	[[ -n "$SUITE_FILE" && -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || usage "missing or unreadable --suite-file"
    79	[[ -n "$RUN_DIR" || -n "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "one of --run-dir or --batch-dir is required"
    80	[[ -z "$RUN_DIR" || -z "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "--run-dir and --batch-dir are exclusive"
    81	SUITE_JSON="$(yq -o=json '.' "$SUITE_FILE")" || usage "suite file does not parse"
    82	
    83	# ---- rule helpers: each sets EVID and returns 0 (OK) / 1 (FAIL) --------------------
    84	EVID=""
    85	argv_files() { local f; for f in "$R/meta"/phase-*.argv.json; do [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$f"; done; return 0; }
    86	envelope() {  # envelope <gate> → path or empty
    87	  local f="$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-$1.json"
    88	  [[ -f "$f" ]] || f="$R/eval/adversarial-$1.json"
    89	  [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s' "$f"; return 0
    90	}
    91	
    92	expected_labels() {  # the arm's phase set for this run's task type (pipeline-run.sh's plan)
    93	  local type kind
    94	  type="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
    95	  if [[ "$type" == review-catch ]]; then kind=review-catch; else kind=build; fi
    96	  jq -r -n --argjson arm "$ARM_DEF" --argjson suite "$SUITE_JSON" --arg kind "$kind" \
    97	    --argjson tg "$(jq -c '.arm_toggles // {}' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" '
    98	    (if $kind == "review-catch" then ["REVIEW","AUDIT"] else ["PLAN","IMPLEMENT","REVIEW","FIX","AUDIT","FIX"] end) as $dflt
    99	    | ($arm.phases // $suite.phase_sets[$kind] // $dflt) as $p0
   100	    | (if ($tg.loa_mount == false) then ["BARE"] else $p0 end) as $p1
   101	    | (if ($tg.sprint_plan == false) then ($p1 | map(select(. != "PLAN"))) else $p1 end) as $p2
   102	    | (if ($tg.gates == false) and ($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) != null then $p2[0:(($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) + 1)] else $p2 end) as $p3
   103	    | reduce $p3[] as $n ({out: [], fix: 0};
   104	        if $n == "FIX" then .fix += 1 | .out += ["FIX" + (.fix | tostring)] else .out += [$n] end)
   105	    | .out | join(",")'
   106	}

   108	rule_no_dot_claude() {
   109	  if [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" || -e "$R/sandbox/CLAUDE.md" ]]; then EVID="sandbox has .claude/ or CLAUDE.md"; return 1; fi
   110	  EVID="sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md"
   111	}
   112	rule_no_system_prompt() {
   113	  local f n=0 hit=""
   114	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   115	    n=$((n + 1))
   116	    jq -e '(.argv // []) | index("--append-system-prompt-file") != null' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && hit="$hit $(basename "$f")"
   117	  done < <(argv_files)
   118	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no phase argv captured"; return 1; }
   119	  [[ -z "$hit" ]] || { EVID="--append-system-prompt-file in$hit"; return 1; }
   120	  EVID="no --append-system-prompt-file in $n argv"
   121	}
   122	rule_no_audit_rows() {
   123	  [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl" ]] && { EVID="sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl exists"; return 1; }
   124	  EVID="no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl"
   125	}
   126	rule_all_phases_present() {
   127	  local want got st
   128	  want="$(expected_labels)"
   129	  got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   130	  st="$(jq -r '.status // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   131	  if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then EVID="phases $got"; return 0; fi
   132	  case "$st" in
   133	    cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted|running)
   134	      if [[ -n "$got" && ",$want," == ",$got,"* ]]; then EVID="phases $got (run stopped: $st; set $want)"; return 0; fi ;;
   135	  esac
   136	  EVID="phases ${got:-none}, want $want (status $st)"; return 1
   137	}
   138	rule_no_plan_phase() {
   139	  local n; n="$(jq '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN")] | length' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   140	  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n PLAN record(s)"; return 1; }

   143	rule_one_voice_planned() {

   149	                elif (.companion_voice | type) == "object" then .companion_voice.planned else "absent" end | tostring' "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo unreadable)"
   150	    ev="$ev $g:planned=$v"

   152	  done
   153	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="companion_voice${bad}"; return 1; }

   156	rule_no_gate_phases() {
   157	  local got; got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" or .name == "AUDIT" or .name == "FIX") | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   158	  [[ -z "$got" ]] || { EVID="gate records $got"; return 1; }
   159	  EVID="no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record"

   161	rule_enforce_env_false() {
   162	  local f n=0 bad=""
   163	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   164	    n=$((n + 1))
   165	    [[ "$(jq -r '.env.LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE // "unset"' "$f")" == false ]] || bad="$bad $(basename "$f" .argv.json)"

   171	rule_no_flatline_rows() {
   172	  local n=0
   173	  if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]; then
   174	    n="$(jq -R -n '[inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object")
   175	           | (.payload.calling_primitive // .calling_primitive // .agent // "") | select(test("^flatline"))] | length' \
   176	         "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl")"

   178	  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n flatline MODELINV row(s)"; return 1; }

   182	rule_implementer_single_session() {
   183	  local ids n sid f bad=""
   184	  ids="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.skipped != true and (.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX")) | .session_id]' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   185	  n="$(jq 'length' <<<"$ids")"
   186	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no implementer record"; return 1; }
   187	  [[ "$(jq '[.[] | select(. == null)] | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="an implementer record has no session_id"; return 1; }
   188	  [[ "$(jq 'unique | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 1 ]] || { EVID="implementer session ids $(jq -r 'unique | join(",")' <<<"$ids")"; return 1; }
   189	  sid="$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$ids")"
   190	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   191	    case "$(jq -r '.name' "$f")" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) ;; *) continue ;; esac
   192	    jq -e '.resume == null' "$f" >/dev/null && continue
   193	    jq -e --arg s "$sid" '.resume == $s and ((.argv | index("--resume")) as $i | $i != null and .argv[$i + 1] == $s)' "$f" >/dev/null \
   194	      || bad="$bad $(jq -r '.label' "$f")"
   195	  done < <(argv_files)
   196	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="continuation argv does not resume $sid:$bad"; return 1; }
   197	  EVID="one session $sid across $n implementer record(s)"
   198	}
   199	rule_gates_separate_sessions() {
   200	  local r a impl
   201	  r="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   202	  a="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "AUDIT" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   203	  impl="$(jq -c '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX") | .session_id | select(. != null)] | unique' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   204	  [[ "$r" != null && "$a" != null ]] || { EVID="gate session ids review=$r audit=$a"; return 1; }
   205	  [[ "$r" != "$a" ]] || { EVID="REVIEW and AUDIT share session $r"; return 1; }
   206	  if jq -e --arg r "$r" --arg a "$a" 'index($r) != null or index($a) != null' <<<"$impl" >/dev/null; then
   207	    EVID="a gate shares an implementer session"; return 1
   208	  fi
   209	  EVID="review $r, audit $a, implementer $(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"$impl")"
   210	}
   211	rule_effort_flag_medium() {
   212	  local f n=0 ok=0
   213	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   214	    n=$((n + 1))
   215	    jq -e '(.argv // []) | (index("--effort")) as $i | $i != null and .[$i + 1] == "medium"' "$f" >/dev/null && ok=$((ok + 1))
   216	  done < <(argv_files)
   217	  [[ $n -gt 0 && $ok -eq $n ]] || { EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"; return 1; }
   218	  EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"
   219	}
   220	rule_skill_effort_stripped() {
   221	  local f n=0 hit=0
   222	  for f in "$R"/sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
   223	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   224	    n=$((n + 1))
   225	    # the YAML frontmatter only (first line `---` to the next `---`); a body line may say effort:
   226	    awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" {exit} NR > 1 && $0 == "---" {exit} NR > 1 && /^effort:/ {hit = 1; exit} END {exit !hit}' "$f" \
   227	      && hit=$((hit + 1))
   228	  done
   229	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no sandbox SKILL.md"; return 1; }
   230	  [[ $hit -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$hit/$n SKILL.md still carry effort:"; return 1; }
   231	  EVID="skill effort lines stripped $n/$n"
   232	}
   233	rule_integrity_clean() {
   234	  local man="$R/sandbox/.claude/checksums.json" msha out
   235	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.arm_toggles.loa_mount' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" == false ]]; then
   236	    [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" ]] && { EVID="loa_mount: false but sandbox has .claude/"; return 1; }
   237	    EVID="no mount (loa_mount: false)"; return 0
   238	  fi
   239	  msha="$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 // empty' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   240	  [[ -n "$msha" && "$msha" != none ]] || { EVID="no arm_evidence.manifest_sha256"; return 1; }
   241	  [[ -f "$man" ]] && jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { EVID="no sandbox .claude/checksums.json files map"; return 1; }
   242	  # one hashlib walk over every manifest entry: "<n> <tampered> <missing> <file-sha> <first problem>"
   243	  out="$(python3 -I -c '
   244	import hashlib, json, os, sys
   245	root, man = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   246	def sha(p):
   247	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   248	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
   249	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
   250	            h.update(b)
   251	    return h.hexdigest()
   252	files = json.load(open(man)).get("files") or {}
   253	bad = missing = 0; first = "-"
   254	for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):
   255	    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
   256	    if not os.path.isfile(p):
   257	        missing += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "missing " + rel
   258	    elif sha(p) != want:
   259	        bad += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "tampered " + rel
   260	print(len(files), bad, missing, sha(man), first)' "$R/sandbox" "$man")" || { EVID="hash walk failed"; return 1; }
   261	  local n bad missing filesha first
   262	  read -r n bad missing filesha first <<<"$out"
   263	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="manifest lists no files"; return 1; }
   264	  if [[ "$bad" -gt 0 || "$missing" -gt 0 ]]; then EVID="$bad tampered, $missing missing of $n ($first)"; return 1; fi
   265	  EVID="$n manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 ${msha:0:12}"
   266	  [[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"
   267	  return 0
   268	}
   269	rule_applicability_refused() {
   270	  local f="$R/meta/refused.json" a t
   271	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
   272	    # a run that was not refused: its task type must be one the arm declares
   273	    t="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   274	    local k=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && k=review-catch
   275	    if jq -e --arg k "$k" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   276	         <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   277	      EVID="applicable: $t in task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") (no refusal needed)"; return 0
   278	    fi
   279	    EVID="ran on $t outside task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") without a refusal record"; return 1
   280	  fi
   281	  a="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$f")"; t="$(jq -r '.type // ""' "$f")"
   282	  [[ "$a" == "$ARM" && -n "$t" ]] || { EVID="refusal record names arm '$a' type '$t'"; return 1; }
   283	  local kind=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && kind=review-catch
   284	  if jq -e --arg k "$kind" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   285	       <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   286	    EVID="arm task_types $(jq -c '.task_types' <<<"$ARM_DEF") include $t, yet the run was refused"; return 1
   287	  fi
   288	  EVID="refused $t (task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF"))"
   289	}

   291	# ---- one run ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   292	check_run() {  # check_run <run-dir> → prints lines; returns 0/1; 2 on usage problems
   293	  R="$1"
   294	  local arm rules rule fails=0 total=0 results='[]' ok
   295	  if [[ -n "$ARM_OPT" ]]; then arm="$ARM_OPT"
   296	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/arm" ]]; then arm="$(sed -n '1p' "$R/meta/arm" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   297	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/refused.json")"
   298	  else arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
   299	  [[ -n "$arm" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no arm for $R" >&2; return 2; }
   300	  ARM="$arm"
   301	  ARM_DEF="$(jq -c --arg a "$arm" '[.arms // [] | .[] | select(.id == $a)][0] // empty' <<<"$SUITE_JSON")"
   302	  [[ -n "$ARM_DEF" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm is not declared in the suite" >&2; return 2; }
   303	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$ARM_DEF")" == true ]]; then
   304	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: true, absent: true, rules: []}'
   305	    else printf 'arm %s: absent (component-absent; no rules)\n' "$arm"; fi
   306	    return 0
   307	  fi
   308	  if [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then
   309	    rules="applicability_refused"
   310	  else
   311	    [[ -f "$R/meta/pipeline.json" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no meta/pipeline.json under $R" >&2; return 2; }
   312	    rules="$(jq -r '(.took_effect // []) | .[]' <<<"$ARM_DEF")"
   313	    [[ -n "$rules" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm lists no took_effect rules" >&2; return 2; }
   314	  fi
   315	  while IFS= read -r rule; do
   316	    [[ -n "$rule" ]] || continue
   317	    total=$((total + 1)); EVID=""
   318	    if declare -F "rule_$rule" >/dev/null; then
   319	      if "rule_$rule"; then ok=true; else ok=false; fi
   320	    else
   321	      ok=false; EVID="unknown rule id"
   322	    fi
   323	    [[ "$ok" == true ]] || fails=$((fails + 1))
   324	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
   325	      results="$(jq -c --arg r "$rule" --argjson ok "$ok" --arg e "$EVID" '. + [{rule: $r, ok: $ok, evidence: $e}]' <<<"$results")"
   326	    else
   327	      printf 'arm %s: %s %s %s\n' "$arm" "$rule" "$([[ "$ok" == true ]] && echo OK || echo FAIL)" "$EVID"
   328	    fi
   329	  done <<<"$rules"
   330	  if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
   331	    jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" --argjson rules "$results" --argjson ok "$([[ $fails -eq 0 ]] && echo true || echo false)" \
   332	      '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: $ok, rules: $rules}'
   333	  elif [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]; then
   334	    printf 'arm %s: OK\n' "$arm"
   335	  else
   336	    printf 'arm %s: FAIL (%d of %d rules)\n' "$arm" "$fails" "$total"
   337	  fi
   338	  [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]
   339	}
   340	
   341	if [[ -n "$RUN_DIR" ]]; then
   342	  [[ -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] || usage "run dir not found: $RUN_DIR"
   343	  rc=0; check_run "$RUN_DIR" || rc=$?
   344	  exit "$rc"
   345	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/check-loa-mount-scope.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 #1267,
     5	# AC-1.2/AC-1.3; SDD §5.3). check-loa.sh check_integrity classifies every
     6	# manifest path as ok, Tampered (fail), not-mounted (a submodule mount does
     7	# not link it but .loa/<path> has it: counted, one summary line, never a
     8	# failure) or Missing (fail).
     9	#
    10	# Seam: check-loa.sh already guards `main` behind
    11	#   [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]
    12	# so each case sources the script in a child bash inside the fixture
    13	# directory and calls check_integrity alone; the child exits 1 when the
    14	# FAILURES counter is non-zero, the same rule main applies. No other check
    15	# runs, and the script is not modified for the test.
    16	# =============================================================================
    17	
    18	setup() {
    19	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    20	  CHECK="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh"
    21	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cloams.XXXXXX")"
    22	  D="$T/downstream"
    23	  # upstream tree inside the submodule path
    24	  mkdir -p "$D/.loa/.claude/lib" "$D/.claude"
    25	  printf 'echo a\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/a.sh"
    26	  printf 'echo b\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh"
    27	  printf 'echo c\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh"
    28	  # the mount links a.sh only (b.sh and lib/c.sh are not linked)
    29	  ln -s ../.loa/.claude/a.sh "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    30	  printf 'aleph:\n  enabled: false\n' > "$D/.loa.config.yaml"
    31	  source "$ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    32	  HA="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/a.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    33	  HB="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    34	  HC="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    35	  write_manifest
    36	}
    37	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    38	
    39	# write_manifest [extra-path hash]... — a/b/lib/c plus any extra pairs
    40	write_manifest() {
    41	  local args=(--arg a "$HA" --arg b "$HB" --arg c "$HC")
    42	  local filter='{".claude/a.sh": $a, ".claude/b.sh": $b, ".claude/lib/c.sh": $c}'
    43	  if [[ $# -ge 2 ]]; then
    44	    args+=(--arg xp "$1" --arg xh "$2")
    45	    filter="$filter + {(\$xp): \$xh}"
    46	  fi
    47	  jq -n "${args[@]}" "{generated: \"2026-10-15T00:00:00Z\", algorithm: \"sha256\", files: ($filter)}" \
    48	    > "$D/.claude/checksums.json"
    49	}
    50	
    51	run_integrity() {
    52	  run bash -c 'cd "$1" && source "$2" && check_integrity && echo "FAILURES=$FAILURES" && [[ $FAILURES -eq 0 ]]' \
    53	    _ "$D" "$CHECK"
    54	}
    55	
    56	@test "CM-1 paths in the upstream tree but not linked are not-mounted; exit unaffected" {
    57	  run_integrity
    58	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    59	  [[ "$output" == *"not-mounted: 2 path(s) exist in the upstream tree but are not linked by this mount"* ]]
    60	  [[ "$output" == *"Integrity verified"* ]]
    61	  [[ "$output" != *"Missing:"* ]]
    62	  [[ "$output" != *"Tampered:"* ]]
    63	  [ "$(grep -c 'not-mounted:' <<< "$output")" -eq 1 ]
    64	}
    65	
    66	@test "CM-2 a present file whose hash differs is Tampered and fails" {
    67	  rm -f "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    68	  printf 'echo tampered\n' > "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    69	  run_integrity
    70	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    71	  [[ "$output" == *"Tampered: .claude/a.sh"* ]]
    72	  [[ "$output" != *"Integrity verified"* ]]
    73	  [[ "$output" == *"FAILURES=1"* ]]
    74	}
    75	
    76	@test "CM-3 a path absent locally and upstream is Missing and fails" {
    77	  write_manifest .claude/gone.sh "$HA"
    78	  run_integrity
    79	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    80	  [[ "$output" == *"Missing: .claude/gone.sh"* ]]
    81	  [[ "$output" == *"not-mounted: 2 path(s)"* ]]
    82	  [[ "$output" != *"Integrity verified"* ]]
    83	}
    84	
    85	@test "CM-4 without a .loa/ submodule an absent path is Missing" {
    86	  find "$D/.loa" -mindepth 1 -delete
    87	  rmdir "$D/.loa"
    88	  printf 'echo a\n' > "$D/.claude/a.sh.real"
    89	  rm -f "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    90	  mv "$D/.claude/a.sh.real" "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    91	  run_integrity
    92	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    93	  [[ "$output" == *"Missing: .claude/b.sh"* ]]
    94	  [[ "$output" == *"Missing: .claude/lib/c.sh"* ]]
    95	  [[ "$output" != *"not-mounted"* ]]
    96	}
    97	
    98	@test "CM-5 every path linked and matching: Integrity verified, no not-mounted line" {
    99	  ln -s ../.loa/.claude/b.sh "$D/.claude/b.sh"
   100	  mkdir -p "$D/.claude/lib"
   101	  ln -s ../../.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh "$D/.claude/lib/c.sh"
   102	  run_integrity
   103	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   104	  [[ "$output" == *"Integrity verified"* ]]
   105	  [[ "$output" != *"not-mounted"* ]]
   106	}
   107	
   108	@test "CM-6 no checksums file: warn and skip, no failure" {
   109	  rm -f "$D/.claude/checksums.json"
   110	  run_integrity
   111	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   112	  [[ "$output" == *"No checksums file - skipping integrity check"* ]]
   113	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1, AC-1.1/AC-1.2;
     5	# SDD §5.1). tools/gen-checksums.sh writes .claude/checksums.json from the
     6	# TRACKED .claude/ tree only: untracked build/cache/runtime artefacts
     7	# (__pycache__, .run/, node_modules) and .claude/overrides/ never enter it.
     8	# Every case runs on a fixture git repository built in setup(); the live
     9	# manifest is only read by GC-8.
    10	# =============================================================================
    11	
    12	setup() {
    13	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    14	  GEN="$ROOT/tools/gen-checksums.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gencs.XXXXXX")"
    16	  R="$T/repo"
    17	  mkdir -p "$R/.claude/scripts/lib" "$R/.claude/overrides" "$R/.claude/scripts/__pycache__" \
    18	    "$R/.claude/.run" "$R/.claude/node_modules/pkg"
    19	  printf 'echo a\n' > "$R/.claude/scripts/a.sh"
    20	  printf 'echo c\n' > "$R/.claude/scripts/lib/c.sh"
    21	  printf 'doc\n' > "$R/.claude/README.md"
    22	  printf 'override\n' > "$R/.claude/overrides/o.md"
    23	  printf 'outside\n' > "$R/outside.txt"
    24	  # untracked artefacts that a working-tree walk would pick up
    25	  printf 'bytecode' > "$R/.claude/scripts/__pycache__/x.pyc"
    26	  printf 'lock' > "$R/.claude/.run/a.lock"
    27	  printf '{}' > "$R/.claude/node_modules/pkg/index.js"
    28	  git -C "$R" init --quiet
    29	  git -C "$R" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null add .claude/scripts/a.sh .claude/scripts/lib/c.sh \
    30	    .claude/README.md .claude/overrides/o.md outside.txt
    31	  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit --quiet -m fixture
    32	}
    33	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    34	
    35	@test "GC-1 the manifest lists exactly the tracked non-override .claude files" {
    36	  run bash "$GEN" --root "$R"
    37	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    38	  run jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$R/.claude/checksums.json"
    39	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    40	  [ "$output" = $'.claude/README.md\n.claude/scripts/a.sh\n.claude/scripts/lib/c.sh' ]
    41	  [ "$(jq -r '.algorithm' "$R/.claude/checksums.json")" = "sha256" ]
    42	  [[ "$(jq -r '.generated' "$R/.claude/checksums.json")" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]{8}Z$ ]]
    43	}
    44	
    45	@test "GC-2 hashes are sha256_portable digests of the working-tree content" {
    46	  bash "$GEN" --root "$R" 2>/dev/null
    47	  source "$ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    48	  expected="$(cd "$R" && sha256_portable .claude/scripts/a.sh | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    49	  [ "$(jq -r '.files[".claude/scripts/a.sh"]' "$R/.claude/checksums.json")" = "$expected" ]
    50	}
    51	
    52	@test "GC-3 two runs are byte-identical except generated" {
    53	  bash "$GEN" --root "$R" --out "$T/one.json" 2>/dev/null
    54	  sleep 1
    55	  bash "$GEN" --root "$R" --out "$T/two.json" 2>/dev/null
    56	  jq 'del(.generated)' "$T/one.json" > "$T/one.nogen"
    57	  jq 'del(.generated)' "$T/two.json" > "$T/two.nogen"
    58	  cmp "$T/one.nogen" "$T/two.nogen"
    59	  # the raw files differ on the generated line only
    60	  run diff <(grep -v '"generated"' "$T/one.json") <(grep -v '"generated"' "$T/two.json")
    61	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    62	}
    63	
    64	@test "GC-4 --check exits 0 right after generation" {
    65	  bash "$GEN" --root "$R" 2>/dev/null
    66	  run bash "$GEN" --root "$R" --check
    67	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    68	}
    69	
    70	@test "GC-5 --check exits 1 naming a changed tracked file" {
    71	  bash "$GEN" --root "$R" 2>/dev/null
    72	  printf 'echo changed\n' > "$R/.claude/scripts/a.sh"
    73	  run --separate-stderr bash "$GEN" --root "$R" --check
    74	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    75	  [[ "$stderr" == *"changed: .claude/scripts/a.sh"* ]]
    76	}
    77	
    78	@test "GC-6 --check exits 1 naming a deleted tracked file" {
    79	  bash "$GEN" --root "$R" 2>/dev/null
    80	  rm -f "$R/.claude/scripts/lib/c.sh"
    81	  run --separate-stderr bash "$GEN" --root "$R" --check
    82	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    83	  [[ "$stderr" == *"removed: .claude/scripts/lib/c.sh"* ]]
    84	}
    85	
    86	@test "GC-7 exit 2 outside a git repository and on a usage error" {
    87	  mkdir -p "$T/plain/.claude"
    88	  printf 'x\n' > "$T/plain/.claude/x.sh"
    89	  run --separate-stderr bash "$GEN" --root "$T/plain" --check
    90	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    91	  [[ "$stderr" == *"not a git work tree"* ]]
    92	  run bash "$GEN" --bogus
    93	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    94	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
2	# =============================================================================
3	# evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Tasks 1.7 + 1.12
4	# (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6; sprint.md AC-1.7, AC-1.12, AC-1.14; PRD AC-4.x)
5	#
6	# evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh drives Loa's phases as separate CLI sessions in a
7	# sandbox repository. Here the CLI is evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub-pipeline.sh,
8	# docker is fixtures/docker-stub.sh, and the executor runs from a temporary copy of
9	# the harness (make_harness) whose lib/sandbox-mount.sh is fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:
10	# the shipped script sources its library by a literal path only (eval.yml trust
11	# boundary), so there is no environment override to point. The executor runs the CLI under
12	# `env -i`, which strips the stubs' control variables, so each test reaches the
13	# stubs through generated wrappers ($T/claude, $T/docker) that first record the
14	# environment and descriptors the executor gave them, then load $T/stub.env.
15	# =============================================================================
16	
17	setup() {
18	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
19	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
20	  FP="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh"
21	  STUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub-pipeline.sh"
22	  DSTUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/docker-stub.sh"
23	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pr.XXXXXX")"
24	  export LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S=0.1
25	  export LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON='{"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5":{"input_per_mtok":4000000,"output_per_mtok":20000000},"global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1":{"input_per_mtok":10000000,"output_per_mtok":50000000}}'
26	  export LOA_EVAL_CREDS_HOME="$T/home"
27	  : > "$T/stub.env"
28	  make_harness
29	  make_source_tree
30	  cp "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation-runs/suite.yaml" "$T/suite.yaml"   # B's suite file as landed
31	  make_tasks
32	  make_wrappers
33	}
34	
35	teardown() {
36	  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
37	  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
38	  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
39	}
40	
41	make_source_tree() {
42	  local s
43	  mkdir -p "$T/src/.claude/loa" "$T/src/.claude/scripts"
44	  for s in planning-sprints implementing-tasks reviewing-code auditing-security; do
45	    mkdir -p "$T/src/.claude/skills/$s"
46	    printf -- '---\nname: %s\neffort: xhigh\n---\nbody\n' "$s" > "$T/src/.claude/skills/$s/SKILL.md"
47	  done
48	  echo "loa" > "$T/src/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
49	  printf 'flatline_protocol:\n  enabled: true\n  code_review:\n    enabled: true\n  security_audit:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$T/src/.loa.config.yaml"
50	  ( cd "$T/src" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -qm init )
51	  # the operator's credential directories (copied per run in container mode)
52	  mkdir -p "$T/home/.aws" "$T/home/.claude/projects/big" "$T/home/.codex/sessions"
53	  echo "[default]" > "$T/home/.aws/config"
54	  echo "{}" > "$T/home/.claude/settings.json"
55	  echo "history" > "$T/home/.claude/history.jsonl"
56	  echo "{}" > "$T/home/.codex/auth.json"
57	  echo "model = 'x'" > "$T/home/.codex/config.toml"
58	  echo '{"claudeAiOauth": "subscription"}' > "$T/home/.claude/.credentials.json"
59	}
60	
61	# a temporary copy of the harness: the stub mount library sits at the literal path
62	# pipeline-run.sh sources (lib/sandbox-mount.sh)
63	make_harness() {
64	  H="$T/h/evals/harness"
65	  mkdir -p "$H/lib"
66	  cp "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh" "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh" "$H/"
67	  cp -a "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts" "$H/lib/"
68	  cp "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh" "$H/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
69	  PR="$H/pipeline-run.sh"
70	}
71	
72	make_tasks() {
73	  # build task: fixture tree beside a sibling hidden/ directory that must never be copied
74	  local b="$T/suite/tasks/bf-01" r="$T/suite/tasks/rc-01" p="$T/prs/pr-x"
75	  mkdir -p "$b/fx/src" "$b/hidden/tests"
76	  echo 'print(1)' > "$b/fx/src/app.py"
77	  echo 'assert False' > "$b/hidden/tests/test_secret.py"
78	  printf 'Make the app print two.\n' > "$b/TASK.md"
79	  cat > "$b/task.yaml" <<'YAML'
80	id: bf-01
81	schema_version: 1
82	type: bug-fix
83	fixture: fx
84	criterion: "the app prints two"
85	test_command: ["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests"]
86	YAML
87	  # review-catch task: a PR fixture outside the task dir
88	  mkdir -p "$p/base/lib" "$p/head/lib" "$r"
89	  echo 'a=1' > "$p/base/lib/x.sh"; echo 'a=2' > "$p/head/lib/x.sh"
90	  printf -- '--- a/lib/x.sh\n+++ b/lib/x.sh\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-a=1\n+a=2\n' > "$p/head.diff"
91	  printf '# PR\nChange a.\n' > "$p/PR.md"
92	  printf '# Review instructions\nReview it.\n' > "$p/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
93	  printf '# Audit instructions\nAudit it.\n' > "$p/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
94	  printf 'name: pr-x\ndescription: "planted defects live elsewhere"\n' > "$p/fixture.yaml"
95	  printf 'Review the pull request in pr/.\n' > "$r/TASK.md"
96	  cat > "$r/task.yaml" <<YAML

100	fixture: null

104	  BUILD="$b/task.yaml" REVIEWC="$r/task.yaml"
105	}

107	make_wrappers() {
108	  mkdir -p "$T/log" "$T/dlog"
109	  cat > "$T/claude" <<EOF
110	#!/usr/bin/env bash
111	env | sed -E 's/^(AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK)=.*/\1=<set>/' > "$T/log/pending.env"   # key name only, never the value
112	if [[ -n "\${AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK:-}" ]]; then
113	  if [[ "\$AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK" == "\$(cat "$T/token" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then echo match; else echo mismatch; fi >> "$T/log/token.check"

116	set -a; . "$T/stub.env"; set +a

123	[[ -f "$T/docker.env" ]] && { set -a; . "$T/docker.env"; set +a; }

127	}

129	# run_pr <arm> [task-yaml] [extra args…] — host executor unless --executor given
130	run_pr() {

140	# --- plan -------------------------------------------------------------------------

     2	# regen.sh — rebuild the fixture run directories under runs/ (cycle-130 Sprint 258)
     3	#
     4	# Each fixture is a real evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh run (host executor) against
     5	# the stub CLI (../claude-stub-pipeline.sh) and the stub mount library
     6	# (../mount-lib-stub.sh), using suite.yaml and the tasks under tasks/. The sandbox's
     7	# own .git and the snapshot bundles are dropped (no nested repositories in the
     8	# tracked tree); absolute paths are rewritten to /fixture and /home/operator.
     9	# grade.json files and MANIFEST.json are written here as Sprint 259's grader and
    10	# run-ablation.sh would shape them (SDD §3.4, §3.6).

    17	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

    65	  if [[ -d "$GEN/runs/$name/sandbox/.git" ]]; then find "$GEN/runs/$name/sandbox/.git" -depth -delete; fi

    68	}

    99	{"hidden_tests": null, "regressions": null,
   100	 "recall": {"defects_seeded": 3, "defects_caught": 2, "recall": 0.6667, "flags": 4}, "false_positives": 1,

   103	 "diff_lines": null, "files_changed": null, "contaminated": null, "grader_version": "1"}
   104	JSON

   106	        suite_version: 1, fingerprint: "fp:fixture", image_digest: "sha256:fixture-image", executor_mode: "host",
   107	        agy_opt_in: false,
   108	        arm_map: {"abl-fixture-a1_full-bf-01-t1": "a1_full", "abl-fixture-a0_bare-bf-01-t1": "a0_bare",
   109	                  "abl-fixture-a2_no_sprint_plan-bf-01-t1": "a2_no_sprint_plan", "abl-fixture-a3_one_voice-rc-01-t1": "a3_one_voice",
   110	                  "abl-fixture-a4_no_gates-bf-01-t1": "a4_no_gates", "abl-fixture-a5_no_flatline-bf-01-t1": "a5_no_flatline",

# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Runs BATS test suites for shell scripts and framework infrastructure.
# Two test directories:

#   - .claude/scripts/tests/ — Script-level tests (20 files)

# Triggers on changes to shell scripts, test files, or this workflow.
#
# PINNING POLICY: All external dependencies are pinned to specific versions
# with integrity verification. This prevents supply-chain attacks where a
# compromised "latest" release silently poisons CI. To rotate:
#   1. Update the version and download URL
#   2. Recompute SHA256: wget -qO- <url> | sha256sum
#   3. Update the checksum in the verification step
