1	# Copy of evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml as implementer B landed it (Sprint 258); the fixture runs and
     2	# evals/tests/{pipeline-run,ablation-row,took-effect}.bats read this copy so the tests do not move with the live suite.
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
     5	#
     6	# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
     7	# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
     8	# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
     9	# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
    10	#
    11	# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
    12	# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
    13	# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
    14	# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
    15	# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
    16	# task_types against the known types).
    17	#
    18	# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
    19	#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
    20	#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
    21	# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
    22	#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
    23	#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
    24	# =============================================================================
    25	name: ablation-2.0
    26	version: 1
    27	source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
    28	agy_opt_in: false
    29	tasks:
    30	  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
    31	  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
    32	  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
    33	suite_version: 1
    34	trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
    35	cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
    36	caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
    37	priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
    38	cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)
    39	
    40	# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
    41	# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
    42	phase_defaults:
    43	  models:
    44	    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    45	    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    46	    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    47	    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    48	    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
    49	    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
    50	  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 40, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 40, BARE: 170}
    51	  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 20, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 20, BARE: 70}
    52	  tools: "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"   # identical for every arm, A0 included
    53	phase_sets:   # D-4.1: A1's phases per task type; FIX runs only after a CHANGES_REQUIRED gate
    54	  review-catch: [REVIEW, AUDIT]
    55	  build: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX]
    56	
    57	arms:
    58	  - {id: a0_bare, label: A0, task_types: [all], toggles: {loa_mount: false}, phases: [BARE], effort: high,
    59	     took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]}
    60	  - {id: a1_full, label: A1, task_types: [all], toggles: {}, took_effect: [all_phases_present, integrity_clean]}
    61	  - {id: a2_no_sprint_plan, label: A2, task_types: [build], toggles: {sprint_plan: false},
    62	     phases: [IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX],
    63	     took_effect: [no_plan_phase, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
    64	  - {id: a3_one_voice, label: A3, task_types: [all], toggles: {companion_voice: false}, took_effect: [one_voice_planned, integrity_clean]}
    65	  - {id: a4_no_gates, label: A4, task_types: [build], toggles: {gates: false},
    66	     phases: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT],
    67	     took_effect: [no_gate_phases, enforce_env_false, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}   # build only: on a review-catch task the gates are the task (DEC-0400)
    68	  - {id: a5_no_flatline, label: A5, task_types: [build], toggles: {flatline: false},
    69	     took_effect: [no_flatline_rows, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
    70	  - {id: a6_one_window, label: A6, task_types: [build], toggles: {context_resets: false},
    71	     took_effect: [implementer_single_session, gates_separate_sessions, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
    72	  - {id: a7_effort_medium, label: A7, task_types: [all], toggles: {effort: medium},
    73	     took_effect: [effort_flag_medium, skill_effort_stripped, integrity_clean]}
    74	  - {id: a8_no_ceremonies, label: A8, absent: true,
    75	     evidence: "no /meeting command, skill or sosyete config key at 4d69c3c4 (grep -rli sosyete .claude/ docs/; ls .claude/commands .claude/skills)"}
    76	
    77	rules:   # D-A5: pre-registered, mirrored in NOTES
    78	  threshold_points: 0.03
    79	  cost_lower_pct: 15
    80	  bootstrap: {resamples: 10000, level: 0.90, paired: true, units: {hidden_test_pass_rate: tasks, defect_catch_rate: defects}, also_report: {defect_catch_rate: tasks}}   # DEC-0399
    81	  primaries_by_arm: {build_only: [hidden_test_pass_rate], all_types: [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate]}   # DEC-0400
    82	  cap_failure: counts_as_failed            # 0 on each applicable primary (DEC-0393)
    83	  exclusion: {statuses: [degraded, contaminated, interrupted], mode: pairwise, inconclusive_above_share: 0.25}
    84	  sensitivity_figure: cap_failures_excluded  # printed, never decides
    85	  multiple_comparisons: none                 # expected false positives at 0.90 over 6 components printed
    86	  drift_guard: {cli_version: fixed_per_batch, model_ids: fixed_per_batch}   # DEC-0407

# =============================================================================
# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
#
# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
#
# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
# task_types against the known types).
#
# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
# =============================================================================
name: ablation-2.0
version: 1
source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
agy_opt_in: false
tasks:
  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
suite_version: 1
trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)

# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
phase_defaults:
  models:
    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 40, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 40, BARE: 170}
  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 20, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 20, BARE: 70}
  tools: "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"   # identical for every arm, A0 included
phase_sets:   # D-4.1: A1's phases per task type; FIX runs only after a CHANGES_REQUIRED gate
  review-catch: [REVIEW, AUDIT]
  build: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX]

arms:
  - {id: a0_bare, label: A0, task_types: [all], toggles: {loa_mount: false}, phases: [BARE], effort: high,
     took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a1_full, label: A1, task_types: [all], toggles: {}, took_effect: [all_phases_present, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a2_no_sprint_plan, label: A2, task_types: [build], toggles: {sprint_plan: false},
     phases: [IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX],
     took_effect: [no_plan_phase, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a3_one_voice, label: A3, task_types: [all], toggles: {companion_voice: false}, took_effect: [one_voice_planned, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a4_no_gates, label: A4, task_types: [build], toggles: {gates: false},
     phases: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT],
     took_effect: [no_gate_phases, enforce_env_false, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}   # build only: on a review-catch task the gates are the task (DEC-0400)
  - {id: a5_no_flatline, label: A5, task_types: [build], toggles: {flatline: false},
     took_effect: [no_flatline_rows, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a6_one_window, label: A6, task_types: [build], toggles: {context_resets: false},
     took_effect: [implementer_single_session, gates_separate_sessions, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a7_effort_medium, label: A7, task_types: [all], toggles: {effort: medium},
     took_effect: [effort_flag_medium, skill_effort_stripped, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a8_no_ceremonies, label: A8, absent: true,
     evidence: "no /meeting command, skill or sosyete config key at 4d69c3c4 (grep -rli sosyete .claude/ docs/; ls .claude/commands .claude/skills)"}

rules:   # D-A5: pre-registered, mirrored in NOTES
  threshold_points: 0.03
  cost_lower_pct: 15
  bootstrap: {resamples: 10000, level: 0.90, paired: true, units: {hidden_test_pass_rate: tasks, defect_catch_rate: defects}, also_report: {defect_catch_rate: tasks}}   # DEC-0399
  primaries_by_arm: {build_only: [hidden_test_pass_rate], all_types: [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate]}   # DEC-0400
  cap_failure: counts_as_failed            # 0 on each applicable primary (DEC-0393)
  exclusion: {statuses: [degraded, contaminated, interrupted], mode: pairwise, inconclusive_above_share: 0.25}
  sensitivity_figure: cap_failures_excluded  # printed, never decides
  multiple_comparisons: none                 # expected false positives at 0.90 over 6 components printed
  drift_guard: {cli_version: fixed_per_batch, model_ids: fixed_per_batch}   # DEC-0407
  order: trial_major_seeded_shuffle_within_block
  took_effect_per_trial: true                # a miss → infrastructure_error, arm paused until --clear-arm (DEC-0418)
  predicates:                                # DEC-0416; d = arm − A1 point estimate, [lo, hi] its 90 % interval, c/w = cost/wall-clock Δ %
    investigate: "any applicable primary has lo > 0"
    keep: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03 and hi < 0"
    inconclusive: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03, or the arm's excluded share > 0.25, or no valid pair"
    remove: "else every applicable primary has d >= -0.03 and (c <= -15 or w <= -15)"
    simplify: "else (every applicable primary within -0.03, cost similar)"
  review_catch: {defect_counts_once_across_gates: true, false_positive_dedupe: cited_region, verdict_accurate_iff: "CHANGES_REQUIRED when the key holds a high or critical defect, APPROVED when none"}   # DEC-0420
  inconclusive_extension_trials: 2
  h1: "a1_full beats a0_bare on at least one primary with the interval excluding zero, else halt before promotion"
  a4_sensitivity: "a4_no_gates worse than a1_full on hidden_test_pass_rate with the interval excluding zero, else harden tasks before acting on other arms"
  decision_states: [investigate, keep, inconclusive, remove, simplify, not_run_cut, inconclusive_by_power]
  mde_cut: 0.10   # sprint Task 3.4: an arm whose MDE at affordable trials exceeds this is pre-declared inconclusive_by_power and not run

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# claude-ablation-stub.sh — wraps evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub.sh for the
     3	# cycle-130 bats (run-arms.bats, arm-toggles.bats). No model call.
     4	#
     5	#   STUB_COST_USD      the result event's total_cost_usd (default: the base stub's
     6	#                      canned transcript is used unchanged)
     7	#   STUB_FULL_ENV_FILE the complete environment (`env`) is written there
     8	#   STUB_CONC_DIR      concurrency probe: each call registers itself in the dir
     9	#                      for STUB_SLEEP seconds and appends the number of calls
    10	#                      running at its start to <dir>.log
    11	#   STUB_SLEEP         seconds to stay registered (default 0)
    12	set -euo pipefail
    13	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    14	BASE="$HERE/../claude-stub.sh"
    15	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" ]]; then exec "$BASE" --version; fi
    16	
    17	if [[ -n "${STUB_FULL_ENV_FILE:-}" ]]; then env > "$STUB_FULL_ENV_FILE"; fi
    18	if [[ -n "${STUB_CONC_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    19	  mkdir -p "$STUB_CONC_DIR"
    20	  : > "$STUB_CONC_DIR/$$"
    21	  ls "$STUB_CONC_DIR" | wc -l | tr -d ' ' >> "$STUB_CONC_DIR.log"
    22	  sleep "${STUB_SLEEP:-0}"
    23	  rm -f "$STUB_CONC_DIR/$$"
    24	fi
    25	if [[ -n "${STUB_COST_USD:-}" ]]; then
    26	  ev="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/stub-events.XXXXXX")"
    27	  cat > "$ev" <<EVENTS
    28	{"type":"system","subtype":"init","model":"claude-sonnet-5"}
    29	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"review.md","content":"r"}}]}}
    30	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"duration_ms":1000,"num_turns":2,"result":"done","total_cost_usd":${STUB_COST_USD},"usage":{"input_tokens":10,"output_tokens":5},"modelUsage":{"claude-sonnet-5-20260401":{"inputTokens":10,"outputTokens":5,"costUSD":${STUB_COST_USD}}}}
    31	EVENTS
    32	  export STUB_EVENTS_FILE="$ev"
    33	fi
    34	exec "$BASE" "$@"
    35	# suite-lib.bash — fixture-suite builders for validate-suite.bats and freeze.bats
    36	# (cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11). Sourced by the bats files; the templates are
    37	# the two committed smoke tasks, so the fixtures follow the real schema.
    38	#
    39	#   make_task <root> <group> <id> <type>   copy a smoke task to <root>/<group>/<id>
    40	#                                          as <type> (build types from smoke-build-01,
    41	#                                          review-catch from smoke-review-01)
    42	#   make_full_suite <root>                 four tasks of each type under tasks/
    43	
    44	SMOKE_ROOT="${SMOKE_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke}"
    45	
    46	make_task() {
    47	  local root="$1" group="$2" id="$3" type="$4" src
    48	  case "$type" in review-catch) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-review-01" ;; *) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-build-01" ;; esac
    49	  mkdir -p "$root/$group"
    50	  cp -a "$src" "$root/$group/$id"
    51	  local ty="$root/$group/$id/task.yaml"
    52	  ID="$id" TY="$type" yq -i '.id = strenv(ID) | .type = strenv(TY)' "$ty"
    53	  if [[ "$type" != "review-catch" ]]; then
    54	    FX="$group/$id/fixture" yq -i '.fixture = strenv(FX)' "$ty"
    55	  fi
    56	  if [[ "$type" == "refactor" ]]; then
    57	    printf 'def test_structure():\n    assert True\n' > "$root/$group/$id/hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"
    58	    yq -i '.structural_check = "hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"' "$ty"
    59	  fi
    60	}
    61	
    62	make_full_suite() {
    63	  local root="$1" ty i
    64	  for ty in feature-build bug-fix refactor review-catch; do
    65	    for i in 1 2 3 4; do make_task "$root" tasks "$ty-0$i" "$ty"; done
    66	  done
    67	}

+
+# --- cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.6 (PRD AC-3.1, AC-3.2, AC-5.6; sprint AC-1.6, AC-1.10;
+# DEC-0421, DEC-0431, DEC-0433). The ablation-2.0 arms through execute-agent.sh, and
+# lib/sandbox-mount.sh called directly for the pipeline-shaped (whole-tree) mount.
+
+ABL_SUITE_REL="evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
+LIB_REL="evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
+
+lib() {  # lib <function> <args…> — one library call in a strict subshell
+  bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source "$1"; shift; "$@"' _ "$REPO_ROOT/$LIB_REL" "$@"
+}
+
+# The prompt tree as the pipeline mounts it: a catalog with two default_effort
+# entries and its .checksum, a second skill with an effort line, the beads
+# state script, and an overrides/ file the manifest must skip.
+extend_tree() {
+  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/defaults" "$PT/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks" "$PT/.claude/scripts/beads" "$PT/.claude/overrides"
+  printf '%s\n' "providers:" "  anthropic:" "    models:" "      claude-opus-5-5:" "        params:" "          default_effort: high" \
+    "      claude-fable-5-1:" "        params:" "          default_effort: xhigh" > "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml"
+  sha256sum_of "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" > "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum"
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: implementing-tasks" "effort: xhigh" "model: opus" "---" "# Implement" "effort: this body line stays" \
+    > "$PT/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  cp "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh" "$PT/.claude/scripts/beads/"
+  echo "operator override" > "$PT/.claude/overrides/local.md"
+}
+sha256sum_of() { bash -c 'source "$1"; sha256_portable "$2" | cut -d" " -f1' _ "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" "$1"; }
+
+# check-loa.sh's own integrity check, run inside the sandbox (its cwd-relative manifest)
+integrity_in() {
+  ( cd "$1" && bash -c 'source "$1" && { check_integrity || true; } && echo "FAILURES=$FAILURES"' _ "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh" )
+}
+
+@test "AT-13 ablation-2.0 declares the nine canonical arms, task_types per arm, A8 absent with its evidence, integrity_clean on every runnable arm (AC-1.10)" {
+  S="$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL"
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$S")" = "a0_bare,a1_full,a2_no_sprint_plan,a3_one_voice,a4_no_gates,a5_no_flatline,a6_one_window,a7_effort_medium,a8_no_ceremonies" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.arms[] | select((.task_types | join(",")) == "build") | .id] | join(",")' "$S")" = "a2_no_sprint_plan,a4_no_gates,a5_no_flatline,a6_one_window" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.arms[] | select((.task_types | join(",")) == "all") | .id] | join(",")' "$S")" = "a0_bare,a1_full,a3_one_voice,a7_effort_medium" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.arms[] | select(.id == "a8_no_ceremonies") | .absent' "$S")" = "true" ]
+  yq -r '.arms[] | select(.id == "a8_no_ceremonies") | .evidence' "$S" | grep -q 'grep -rli sosyete .claude/ docs/'
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.arms[] | select(.absent != true) | select((.took_effect // []) | contains(["integrity_clean"]) | not)] | length' "$S")" = "0" ]
+  [ "$(yq -o=json -I=0 '.arms[] | select(.id == "a0_bare") | [.toggles, .phases, .effort]' "$S")" = '[{"loa_mount":false},["BARE"],"high"]' ]
+  [ "$(yq -o=json -I=0 '.arms[] | select(.id == "a7_effort_medium") | .toggles' "$S")" = '{"effort":"medium"}' ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.phase_defaults.max_turns.BARE, .phase_defaults.timeout_min.BARE, .phase_defaults.models.REVIEW' "$S" | tr '\n' ,)" = "170,70,global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1," ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.phase_sets.build | join(",")' "$S")" = "PLAN,IMPLEMENT,REVIEW,FIX,AUDIT,FIX" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.rules.decision_states | length' "$S")" = "7" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.rules.predicates | keys | join(",")' "$S")" = "investigate,keep,inconclusive,remove,simplify" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.caps | [.cycle_usd, .run_usd, .reserve_usd] | join(",")' "$S")" = "1500,12,250" ]
+  # resolve_arm_toggles: absent and undeclared are refused; a1_full and an undeclared baseline are {}
+  run lib resolve_arm_toggles a8_no_ceremonies "$S"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; grep -q 'declared absent' <<<"$output"
+  run lib resolve_arm_toggles a9_nope "$S"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; grep -q 'not declared' <<<"$output"
+  run lib resolve_arm_toggles a1_full "$S"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "{}" ]
+  run lib resolve_arm_toggles a0_bare "$S"
+  [ "$output" = '{"loa_mount":false}' ]
+  run lib resolve_arm_toggles baseline "$S"
+  [ "$output" = "{}" ]
+  # the cycle-129 suites still resolve through ab.arms[]
+  run lib resolve_arm_toggles no_rule_files "$REVIEW_SUITE"
+  [ "$output" = '{"rule_files":false}' ]
+}
+
+@test "AT-14 a0_bare: no .claude/, CLAUDE.md or .loa.config.yaml at executor start, no --append-system-prompt-file, the task prompt only; skill effort is not read" {
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "effort: xhigh" "---" "# Review" > "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
+  export STUB_ARGV_FILE="$T/argv"
+  run_arm a0_bare "$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL" reviewing-code
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ -d "$SNAP" ]
+  [ ! -e "$SNAP/.claude" ] && [ ! -e "$SNAP/CLAUDE.md" ] && [ ! -e "$SNAP/.loa.config.yaml" ] && [ ! -e "$SNAP/system-prompt.md" ]
+  [ ! -e "$WS/.claude" ] && [ ! -e "$WS/CLAUDE.md" ] && [ ! -e "$WS/.eval/skill-prompt.md" ]
+  ! grep -qx -- '--append-system-prompt-file' "$T/argv"
+  ! grep -qx -- '--effort' "$T/argv"
+  grep -qxF 'Read the instructions and carry them out.' "$T/argv"
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.loa_mount' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = "none" ]
+  [ "$(jq -c '.arm_toggles' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = '{"loa_mount":false}' ]
+  # a sandbox that already holds a mount-owned path cannot take the toggle: exit 2, no CLI call
+  rm -rf "$SNAP"; mkdir -p "$WS/.claude"
+  run_arm a0_bare "$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL" reviewing-code
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  [ ! -e "$SNAP" ]
+}
+
+@test "AT-15 a7_effort_medium through execute-agent: --effort medium on argv (over EVAL_EFFORT and the skill's own effort), no effort: in the sandbox SKILL.md frontmatter" {
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "effort: xhigh" "---" "# Review" > "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
+  export STUB_ARGV_FILE="$T/argv"
+  EVAL_EFFORT=low run_arm a7_effort_medium "$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL" reviewing-code
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(grep -x -A1 -- '--effort' "$T/argv" | tail -1)" = "medium" ]
+  [ "$(grep -cx -- '--effort' "$T/argv")" -eq 1 ]
+  ! grep -q '^effort:' "$SNAP/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
+  grep -q '^effort: xhigh' "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
+  E="$WS/.eval/executor.json"
+  [ "$(jq -r '.effort' "$E")" = "medium" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.effort' "$E")" = "medium" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.effort_skills_stripped' "$E")" = "1/1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.effort_catalog' "$E")" = "absent" ]
+}
+
+@test "AT-16 a7 on the whole-tree mount: every SKILL.md frontmatter stripped (body kept), every catalog default_effort medium, .checksum refreshed" {
+  extend_tree
+  W2="$T/ws2"; mkdir -p "$W2"
+  run lib mount_prompt_surface "$W2" "$PT" -
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "mount=tree" ]
+  [ -f "$W2/.loa.config.yaml" ] && [ -f "$W2/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md" ] && [ -f "$W2/.claude/overrides/local.md" ]
+  run lib apply_arm_toggles "$W2" '{"effort":"medium"}' a7_effort_medium
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -qx 'effort=medium' <<<"$output"
+  grep -qx 'effort_skills_stripped=1/3' <<<"$output"
+  grep -qx 'effort_catalog=default_effort=medium in 2 entries; .checksum refreshed' <<<"$output"
+  # grep -L lists every skill: none carries a top-of-line effort: in its frontmatter
+  [ "$(cd "$W2" && grep -L '^effort:' .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "2" ]
+  awk 'NR>1 && $0=="---"{exit} /^effort:/{f=1} END{exit f}' "$W2/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  grep -qx 'effort: this body line stays' "$W2/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  grep -qx 'model: opus' "$W2/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort")) | .default_effort] | unique | join(",")' "$W2/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml")" = "medium" ]
+  [ "$(cat "$W2/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum")" = "$(sha256sum_of "$W2/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml")" ]
+  [ "$(cat "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum")" = "$(sha256sum_of "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml")" ]
+  grep -q 'default_effort: high' "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml"
+  # an unknown effort value cannot take effect
+  run lib apply_arm_toggles "$W2" '{"effort":"turbo"}' x

+}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.1)
#
# execute-agent.sh applies a control arm's toggles to the sandbox copy only.
# Every assertion here reads the sandbox as the EXECUTOR saw it: the CLI stub
# snapshots CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .loa.config.yaml and the appended system
# prompt at the moment it starts (STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR), after every
# materialisation step. The arm ids and toggles come from the real suite
# files; the prompt tree is a synthetic fixture so later prose edits to the
# live kernel cannot change what this test proves.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  EXEC="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh"
  REVIEW_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/review-recall.yaml"
  AUDIT_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/audit-recall.yaml"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/at.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"; SNAP="$T/snap"
  mkdir -p "$WS"
  ( cd "$WS" && git init -q && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init )
  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
  export EVAL_MODEL="claude-fable-5-1"
  export STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR="$SNAP"
  unset LOA_EVAL_ARM LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT EVAL_EFFORT

  # --- synthetic prompt tree (the shape of 864069f2) ---
  PT="$T/tree"
  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/loa" "$PT/.claude/rules" "$PT/.claude/data" \
    "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code" "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security"
  printf '%s\n' "# Loa Framework Instructions" "" "## Three-Zone Model" "" "zones" "" \
    "## Karpathy Principles" "" "Every code-touching turn." "" "1. **Think before coding** — state assumptions." "" \
    "## Process Compliance" "" "rules" > "$PT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  echo "# Git Stash Safety" > "$PT/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
  echo "# Skill Frontmatter Invariants" > "$PT/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "paths:" '  - "grimoires/**"' "---" "# zone state" > "$PT/.claude/rules/zone-state.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "---" "# Review" "Review the diff." > "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: auditing-security" "---" "# Audit" "" "### Coverage" "" \
    "Report every finding you actually observe." "" \
    "Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under" \
    "\`excluded\`, either confirm it or tally it as a finding of your own." "" \
    "## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally" "" "Count every finding." > "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" "  security_audit:" "    enabled: true" > "$PT/.loa.config.yaml"
  ( cd "$PT" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m tree )
  export EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$PT"

  for s in reviewing-code auditing-security; do
    cat > "$T/task-$s.yaml" <<YAML
id: at-$s
schema_version: 1
skill: $s
category: skill-quality
fixture: hello-world-ts
description: "arm toggle task"
prompt: "Read the instructions and carry them out."
agent:
  skill: $s
  artifacts: [review.md]
graders:
  - type: code
    script: file-exists.sh
    args: ["review.md"]
YAML
  done
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

run_arm() {  # run_arm <arm> <suite-file> <skill>
  LOA_EVAL_ARM="$1" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$2" run "$EXEC" --task-yaml "$T/task-$3.yaml" --workspace "$WS"
}

  [ "$(yq -r '[.ab.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$AUDIT_SUITE")" = "baseline,no_audit_delta" ]

1	# suite-lib.bash — fixture-suite builders for validate-suite.bats and freeze.bats
     2	# (cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11). Sourced by the bats files; the templates are
     3	# the two committed smoke tasks, so the fixtures follow the real schema.
     4	#
     5	#   make_task <root> <group> <id> <type>   copy a smoke task to <root>/<group>/<id>
     6	#                                          as <type> (build types from smoke-build-01,
     7	#                                          review-catch from smoke-review-01)
     8	#   make_full_suite <root>                 four tasks of each type under tasks/
     9	
    10	SMOKE_ROOT="${SMOKE_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke}"
    11	
    12	make_task() {
    13	  local root="$1" group="$2" id="$3" type="$4" src
    14	  case "$type" in review-catch) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-review-01" ;; *) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-build-01" ;; esac
    15	  mkdir -p "$root/$group"
    16	  cp -a "$src" "$root/$group/$id"
    17	  local ty="$root/$group/$id/task.yaml"
    18	  ID="$id" TY="$type" yq -i '.id = strenv(ID) | .type = strenv(TY)' "$ty"
    19	  if [[ "$type" != "review-catch" ]]; then
    20	    FX="$group/$id/fixture" yq -i '.fixture = strenv(FX)' "$ty"
    21	  fi
    22	  if [[ "$type" == "refactor" ]]; then
    23	    printf 'def test_structure():\n    assert True\n' > "$root/$group/$id/hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"
    24	    yq -i '.structural_check = "hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"' "$ty"
    25	  fi
    26	}
    27	
    28	make_full_suite() {
    29	  local root="$1" ty i
    30	  for ty in feature-build bug-fix refactor review-catch; do
    31	    for i in 1 2 3 4; do make_task "$root" tasks "$ty-0$i" "$ty"; done
    32	  done
    33	}

jobs:
  bats:
    name: Shell Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # PINNING: SHA verified against actions/checkout v4.3.1 tag
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1

      # cycle-129 FR-1: tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats compares the floor files and
      # corpus rows with origin/main; the depth-1 checkout has no origin/main, so
      # fetch that one ref (no tags) or the floor proof would skip in CI.
      - name: Fetch origin/main for the floor snapshot
        run: git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main

      - name: Configure git identity for tests
        run: |
          git config --global user.name "CI Bot"
          git config --global user.email "ci@example.com"

      # Real Aleph installer fixtures require Node 22 or later.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: '22.22.0'

      # PINNING: SHA matches the actions/setup-python v5.3.0 pin used by
      # cycle099-sprint-1e-tests.yml and jcs-conformance.yml. Rotate together.
      # bug-886: tests/unit/ exercises lib/jcs.sh (rfc8785), trust-store
      # signing (rfc8785 + cryptography), and yaml/schema suites
      # (ruamel.yaml + jsonschema) — without these installs ~22 bats fail.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@0b93645e9fea7318ecaed2b359559ac225c90a2b # v5.3.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - name: Install Python deps for bats suites
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # Pins match cycle099-sprint-1e-tests.yml (ruamel.yaml, jsonschema),
          # the jcs-conformance suite (rfc8785), and ubuntu-latest's
          # cryptography floor. Keep pin sites in sync when rotating.
          # pyyaml: setup-python creates a CLEAN env — the suite's 16+ `import yaml`
          # consumers previously leaned on ubuntu's system python3-yaml (PR #996
          # empirical run: omitting it broke 182 tests). Pin matches
          # cycle099-sprint-2d-c-ts-tests.yml.
          # idna: endpoint-validator's Unicode hostname canonicalization
          # (lib/endpoint-validator.sh:39 requires idna>=3.6) — system python has
          # it, the clean env does not (PR #996 run 2: broke the guarded_curl
          # chain behind call_api / 401-handler suites).
          pip install 'rfc8785==0.1.4' 'jsonschema==4.26.0' 'ruamel.yaml==0.18.17' 'cryptography==46.0.7' 'pyyaml==6.0.2' 'idna==3.10'
          pip install 'pytest==9.0.3' 'httpx==0.28.1'

      # NOTE: yq install step is below (line ~85) and is pre-existing on main.
      # cycle-102 Sprint 1C T1C.1 made yq a hard requirement for the curl-mock
      # harness shim (per BB iter-1 F1/FIND-001: tool absence must be a hard
      # error, never a soft fallback — the prior grep-fallback silently dropped
      # multiline body content). The existing pinned install satisfies this.
      # BB iter-2 BF-001 HIGH was a false positive: the dissenter and reviewer
      # both missed the pre-existing yq install step in the workflow.
      #
      # PINNING: bats-core v1.13.0 — commit SHA verified after clone
      - name: Install bats-core v1.13.0
        run: |
          git clone --branch v1.13.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core
          cd /tmp/bats-core
          expected="3bca150ec86275d6d9d5a4fd7d48ab8b6c6f3d87"
          actual=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: bats-core commit SHA mismatch — expected $expected, got $actual"
            exit 1
          fi
          sudo ./install.sh /usr/local
          bats --version

      - name: Install yq v4.52.4 (pinned + checksum verified)
        run: |
          sudo wget -qO /usr/local/bin/yq https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.52.4/yq_linux_amd64
          echo "0c4d965ea944b64b8fddaf7f27779ee3034e5693263786506ccd1c120f184e8c  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c -
          sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq

      # cycle-129 FR-1: the structural guard register and the generated hooks table
      # must match what guard-yield.sh writes (no audit log is read in --check).
      - name: Guard register drift gate (guard-yield.sh --check)
        run: bash .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --check

      # cycle-129 FR-9 (r256-1 LOW-1): every optional-surface knob is read through
      # profile-lib.sh; a bare `yq '.key // default'` read of a profile key fails here.
      - name: Knob readers go through profile-lib (check-knob-readers.sh)
        run: bash tools/check-knob-readers.sh

content.content:
# 1. Establish project root
    PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)

    # 2. Load integrity enforcement level
    ENFORCEMENT="warn"  # Default
    if [[ -f "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
        ENFORCEMENT=$(grep "^integrity_enforcement:" "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" | awk '{print $2}' || echo "warn")
    fi

    echo "Running pre-flight integrity checks (enforcement: ${ENFORCEMENT})..." >&2

    # 3. Verify System Zone checksums
    if [[ "${ENFORCEMENT}" != "disabled" ]] && [[ -f "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json" ]]; then
        echo "Verifying System Zone integrity..." >&2

        # Simple check: compare file count (full SHA verification would be more thorough)
        EXPECTED_COUNT=$(jq -r '.files | length' "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
        # cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267): the manifest is generated from the TRACKED
        # .claude/ tree (tools/gen-checksums.sh), so count with the same rule:
        # git ls-files -- .claude minus overrides/ and the manifest. In a
        # submodule mount .claude/checksums.json links into the submodule; the
        # count is taken in the tree that owns the manifest.
        MANIFEST_TREE="${PROJECT_ROOT}"
        if [[ -L "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json" ]]; then
            MANIFEST_LINK=$(readlink "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json")
            [[ "${MANIFEST_LINK}" == /* ]] || MANIFEST_LINK="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/${MANIFEST_LINK}"
            MANIFEST_TREE=$(cd "$(dirname "${MANIFEST_LINK}")/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || MANIFEST_TREE="${PROJECT_ROOT}"
        fi
        ACTUAL_COUNT=0
        if git -C "${MANIFEST_TREE}" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ACTUAL_COUNT=$(git -C "${MANIFEST_TREE}" ls-files -- .claude \
                | awk '!/^\.claude\/overrides\// && $0 != ".claude/checksums.json"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
        fi
        # No tracked .claude/ in that tree (outside git, or a standard-mode
        # downstream that does not commit .claude/): keep the legacy count.
        if [[ "${ACTUAL_COUNT}" -eq 0 ]]; then
            ACTUAL_COUNT=$(find "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude" -type f ! -path "*/.git/*" ! -path "*/overrides/*" ! -path "*/checksums.json" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
        fi

        if [[ "${EXPECTED_COUNT}" != "${ACTUAL_COUNT}" ]]; then
            echo "⚠️  System Zone integrity check: file count mismatch" >&2
            echo "   Expected: ${EXPECTED_COUNT} files" >&2
            echo "   Actual:   ${ACTUAL_COUNT} files" >&2

            if [[ "${ENFORCEMENT}" == "strict" ]]; then
                echo "" >&2
                echo "SYSTEM ZONE INTEGRITY VIOLATION" >&2
                echo "" >&2
                echo "The .claude/ directory has been modified outside of the update process." >&2
                echo "" >&2
                echo "Resolution:" >&2
                echo "  1. Move customizations to .claude/overrides/" >&2
                echo "  2. Restore System Zone: .claude/scripts/update.sh --force-restore" >&2
                echo "  3. Re-run operation" >&2
                exit 1
            fi

content.text:
I found no seeded-style logic defects (wrong threshold, inverted check, bad cap arithmetic) in the focus scripts. I checked every header contract against the code: exit codes, the spend `ts >= since` filter, the cap and reserve fallback order (config, then suite, then 1500/250), `headroom = cap - total`, run_id dedup, freeze's sort and hash scope, gen-checksums' exclusions and C-ordered keys, check-loa's ok/Tampered/not-mounted/Missing paths, and the preflight count. All of them match. In a copy under `~/rv` (`/tmp` is mounted noexec here) I ran `spend.bats` (6/6) and `check-loa-mount-scope.bats`. I also ran `gen-checksums.bats`, `check-manifest-paths.bats`, `validate-suite.bats` and `freeze.bats`; those needed a stand-in `compat-lib.sh` and smoke tasks I made up myself, since neither is in the PR tree. Everything passed except the two tests that read committed repo files the PR tree doesn't include (MP-6, FZ-6). The defects below are what's left.

1. **`tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80`** — high confidence. It runs `git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude` without `-z`, so git's default quoting turns any path with non-ASCII bytes or a `"` into a C-quoted string. That string never matches the raw `jq -r keys[]` list, so the file is wrongly reported as untracked. `gen-checksums.sh` (`ls-files -z`) only refuses newline, tab or backslash, so it writes such paths happily. The comment at lines 78-79 claims only newlines are a problem. I reproduced it: tracked files `.claude/café.sh` and `.claude/a"b.sh` give "2 untracked (other=2)", exit 1, right after `gen-checksums.sh` wrote the manifest.

2. **`.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:21-71`** — medium-high confidence. The `push` and `pull_request` path filters were not extended: no `evals/**`, no `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, no `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`, no `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh`. So the new steps (integrity gate at line 175, "Run eval harness tests" at line 212) never run on a PR that only touches the eval harness, its tests, or the new tools. The header at line 5 still says "Two test directories".

3. **`tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:9`** — high confidence. The header says "the live manifest is only read by GC-8", but the file stops at GC-7. The test that checks the committed `.claude/checksums.json` is missing or was dropped.

4. **`evals/tests/freeze.bats:38` and `:79`** — high confidence, but a test-quality issue rather than a script bug. Bash's `set -e` ignores a `! cmd` line that isn't the last command, so `! grep -qv '^[0-9a-f]\{64\}  tasks/'` (FZ-1, the manifest line format) and `! grep -q '  smoke/'` (FZ-4, "without --smoke smoke files are outside the manifest") assert nothing. I confirmed with bats 1.13: a mid-test `! true` doesn't fail. They need `run !` or `[ ... ]`. The same pattern is widespread in `arm-toggles.bats` and `pipeline-run.bats`.

5. **`evals/tests/spend.bats:83-87`** (SP-6) — medium confidence. It claims "the default cap and reserve come from the suite file's caps block", but it only asserts `reserve_usd == 250`, which is also the hard-coded fallback in `spend.sh:81`. It never checks `cap_usd`. It would still pass if the suite-file read (`spend.sh:76`, `:80`) were broken or yq were missing.

6. **Possible, low confidence:** the PR changes several tracked `.claude/` files (`check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `generated-model-maps.sh`, `model-config.yaml`, the bridgebuilder dist files, `CLAUDE.loa.md`) but the diff has no `.claude/checksums.json`. If that manifest is tracked, the new CI gate `gen-checksums.sh --check` (workflow lines 175-178) and MP-6 would fail on drift. The PR says "72 file(s) in scope", so the manifest may simply have been left out of the extract; please check the real branch.

Minor and not worth blocking on: `spend.sh`, `validate-suite.sh` and `freeze.sh` use a bare `shift 2` for value options, so `--cap` with no value exits 1 (from set -e) instead of the documented usage exit 2.

Nothing under `/workspace/pr` was modified.

content.text:
I found no seeded defects. Every file under `head/` and `base/` is byte-identical to the real upstream commit `05442536` (0xHoneyJar/loa, "sprint-258") and its parent, so the defects below are real ones in the original PR. They match what upstream's own follow-up commits `0c200dd6` (review r1) and `ffe162ef` (audit r1) later fixed, and I checked each one myself.

**Tests:** all 73 cases in the four focus bats files pass: took-effect and ablation-row 39/39 against fixtures I rebuilt with `regen.sh`, run-arms and arm-toggles 34/34 at the upstream checkout. Two setup notes:
- `/tmp` here is mounted noexec, so I ran everything from a scratch copy in `$HOME`, since deleted.
- The installed jq 1.6 breaks `pipeline-run.sh` on `{label: $label}`; I used a downloaded jq 1.7.1.

## Defects (head-relative path:line)

1. **`evals/harness/run-arms.sh:506-508` and `:521-523`** (high confidence). The `--max-usd` spend cap does not hold. A trial that dies without reporting a cost (timeout, no result event, no row written) adds `0` to `SPENT`, because the cost falls back via `total_cost_usd // 0` and the no-row branch adds nothing. A batch of runaway or timed-out trials, each possibly near `run_cap`, therefore never moves the cap. My probe run with 5 failing trials and a USD 12 cap launched all 5. Upstream later charges `run_cap` for these trials (`assumed_cap_trials`).

2. **`evals/harness/run-arms.sh:391`, with `:165-167`** (high). The suite aggregate drops batches by directory name (`! -path "$SUITE_DIR/screen-*"`), yet a non-screen `--batch screen-foo` is accepted (it passes the regex at :167). Real results from such a batch silently vanish from the suite-level `STATUS.json`. Upstream later filters on the `screen: true` marker and refuses `screen-*` without `--screen`.

3. **`evals/harness/took-effect.sh:239-240`, `:266`** (high). `integrity_clean` only checks that `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256` exists. A mismatch between it and the sha of `checksums.json` only changes the evidence text at :266; it never FAILs. Files that are not listed in the manifest are never checked. Reproduced: I tampered with `CLAUDE.loa.md`, rewrote its manifest entry and added a new `.claude/loa/extra.md`. The rule reported `integrity_clean OK` with exit 0, even though the recorded sha `8c267cb1…` no longer matched the file's `8994069b…`.

4. **`evals/harness/took-effect.sh:87-88` and `evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:201-202`** (medium-high). The dissent envelope is read from the sandbox first, which the agent can write to, and from `eval/` only as a fallback. An agent-written `adversarial-*.json` can therefore satisfy `one_voice_planned` and spoof `voices_run` and `degraded` in the row. This goes against the stated principle that measurements come from run artefacts, never from what the agent said (took-effect header :8-10; DEC-0413). Upstream later reverses the precedence (audit MEDIUM-A1).

5. **`evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:224-228`** (high). Run-sized inputs (`$PIPE_JSON`, `$MINV`, the envelopes, `$DOT_WRITES`) are passed to jq as `--argjson` strings, which hits Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit. Reproduced: a 216 KB `model-invoke.jsonl` gives "jq: Argument list too long" with exit 126, which is outside the documented exit codes 0/1/2 (:57-60).

6. **`evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:230`, `:247`** (high). Some unexpected input shapes abort jq and the script exits 5, outside the exit contract:
   - At :230, `ms()` calls `fromdateiso8601` without a guard. Reproduced: `started: "2026-10-21T04:04:22+00:00"` gives exit 5, and an empty-string timestamp has the same problem.
   - At :247, `keys` is applied to a non-object `models_used`. Reproduced: exit 5.
   - The same applies to a non-object `verdict_quality` in `voices()` at :231-235.

7. **`evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:247`, contract at :23-24** (medium; this is a design defect). Any `models_used` key other than `model_requested` marks the row `degraded`. Yet `execute-agent.sh:371-373` itself says the CLI's modelUsage includes helper calls such as haiku, which "must not be mis-attributed". So ordinary runs with a helper call get flagged as degraded. Upstream sprint-260 later narrowed this rule to actual substitution.

8. **`evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:212-215`** (low; not a regression against base). An inherited `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE` is unset only in arm mode, so a non-arm or baseline run still passes the operator's override to the executor. Upstream later unsets it in every mode.

**Minor:**
- `evals/tests/run-arms.bats` RA-8 accepts `status 0 || 1`, so a partial screen run still passes.
- `ablation-row.sh:189-190` never checks the arm against `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`, in the writer or in `--validate`; upstream added this check.

Everything else I checked matches its documented contract: the `>` and `<` comparisons, defaults (`run_cap` 12, hint 5.0, 2 screen tasks), field names, the 7 statuses, and the prefix logic.

     6	# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
     7	# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
     8	# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.

    47	ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
    48	RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
    49	    case "$arch" in \

    51	      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
    52	      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
    53	    esac && \
    54	    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
    55	      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
    56	    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
    57	    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
    58	
    59	# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).

    61	      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \

    63	    && npm cache clean --force

    70

#
# Output: `arm <id>: <rule> OK|FAIL <evidence>` per rule, then `arm <id>: OK` or
# `arm <id>: FAIL (<n> of <m> rules)`; --batch-dir adds `took-effect: <runs> runs, <k> failed`.
# --json prints one object per run ({run_dir, arm, ok, rules: [{rule, ok, evidence}]}).
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  every rule OK
#   1  any rule FAIL
#   2  usage error (missing files, unknown arm)
#
# Tested by evals/tests/took-effect.bats (fixture runs under
# evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/).
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
}
rule_no_gate_phases() {
  local got; got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" or .name == "AUDIT" or .name == "FIX") | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  [[ -z "$got" ]] || { EVID="gate records $got"; return 1; }
  EVID="no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record"
}
rule_enforce_env_false() {
  local f n=0 bad=""
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    [[ "$(jq -r '.env.LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE // "unset"' "$f")" == false ]] || bad="$bad $(basename "$f" .argv.json)"
  done < <(argv_files)
  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no phase argv captured"; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE not false in$bad"; return 1; }
  EVID="LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false in $n/$n phase env"
}
rule_no_flatline_rows() {
  local n=0
  if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]; then
    n="$(jq -R -n '[inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object")
           | (.payload.calling_primitive // .calling_primitive // .agent // "") | select(test("^flatline"))] | length' \
         "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl")"
  fi
  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n flatline MODELINV row(s)"; return 1; }
  [[ -f "$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" ]] || { EVID="no flatline rows but no sandbox sprint.md"; return 1; }
  EVID="no flatline MODELINV rows; sprint.md present"
}
rule_implementer_single_session() {
  local ids n sid f bad=""
  ids="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.skipped != true and (.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX")) | .session_id]' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  n="$(jq 'length' <<<"$ids")"
  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no implementer record"; return 1; }
  [[ "$(jq '[.[] | select(. == null)] | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="an implementer record has no session_id"; return 1; }
  [[ "$(jq 'unique | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 1 ]] || { EVID="implementer session ids $(jq -r 'unique | join(",")' <<<"$ids")"; return 1; }
  sid="$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$ids")"
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    case "$(jq -r '.name' "$f")" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    jq -e '.resume == null' "$f" >/dev/null && continue
    jq -e --arg s "$sid" '.resume == $s and ((.argv | index("--resume")) as $i | $i != null and .argv[$i + 1] == $s)' "$f" >/dev/null \
      || bad="$bad $(jq -r '.label' "$f")"
  done < <(argv_files)
  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="continuation argv does not resume $sid:$bad"; return 1; }
  EVID="one session $sid across $n implementer record(s)"
}
rule_gates_separate_sessions() {
  local r a impl
  r="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  a="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "AUDIT" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  impl="$(jq -c '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX") | .session_id | select(. != null)] | unique' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  [[ "$r" != null && "$a" != null ]] || { EVID="gate session ids review=$r audit=$a"; return 1; }
  [[ "$r" != "$a" ]] || { EVID="REVIEW and AUDIT share session $r"; return 1; }
  if jq -e --arg r "$r" --arg a "$a" 'index($r) != null or index($a) != null' <<<"$impl" >/dev/null; then
    EVID="a gate shares an implementer session"; return 1
  fi
  EVID="review $r, audit $a, implementer $(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"$impl")"
}
rule_effort_flag_medium() {
  local f n=0 ok=0
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    jq -e '(.argv // []) | (index("--effort")) as $i | $i != null and .[$i + 1] == "medium"' "$f" >/dev/null && ok=$((ok + 1))
  done < <(argv_files)
  [[ $n -gt 0 && $ok -eq $n ]] || { EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"; return 1; }
  EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"
}
rule_skill_effort_stripped() {
  local f n=0 hit=0
  for f in "$R"/sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    n=$((n + 1))
    # the YAML frontmatter only (first line `---` to the next `---`); a body line may say effort:
    awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" {exit} NR > 1 && $0 == "---" {exit} NR > 1 && /^effort:/ {hit = 1; exit} END {exit !hit}' "$f" \
      && hit=$((hit + 1))
  done
  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no sandbox SKILL.md"; return 1; }
  [[ $hit -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$hit/$n SKILL.md still carry effort:"; return 1; }
  EVID="skill effort lines stripped $n/$n"
}
rule_integrity_clean() {
  local man="$R/sandbox/.claude/checksums.json" msha out
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.arm_toggles.loa_mount' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" == false ]]; then
    [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" ]] && { EVID="loa_mount: false but sandbox has .claude/"; return 1; }
    EVID="no mount (loa_mount: false)"; return 0
  fi
  msha="$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 // empty' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
  [[ -n "$msha" && "$msha" != none ]] || { EVID="no arm_evidence.manifest_sha256"; return 1; }
  [[ -f "$man" ]] && jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { EVID="no sandbox .claude/checksums.json files map"; return 1; }
  # one hashlib walk over every manifest entry: "<n> <tampered> <missing> <file-sha> <first problem>"
  out="$(python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, json, os, sys
root, man = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
def sha(p):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()
files = json.load(open(man)).get("files") or {}
bad = missing = 0; first = "-"
for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):
    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        missing += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "missing " + rel
    elif sha(p) != want:
        bad += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "tampered " + rel
print(len(files), bad, missing, sha(man), first)' "$R/sandbox" "$man")" || { EVID="hash walk failed"; return 1; }

collect() {  # collect <job-id> <arm>
  local jid="$1" arm="$2" i
  i="$(arm_index "$arm")"
  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.flag" ]]; then
    log "corpus drift before $jid: $(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.drift" 2>/dev/null)"
    set_state failed; exit 3
  fi
  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"
    cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" >> "$BATCH_DIR/$arm/results.jsonl"
    local cost
    cost="$(jq -r '(.executor.total_cost_usd // 0) | tonumber? // 0' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [[ "$cost" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$ ]] || cost=0
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$cost")"
    if [[ "$(jq -r '.status' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")" == "completed" ]]; then
      ARM_SUM[$i]="$(fadd "${ARM_SUM[$i]}" "$cost")"; ARM_N[$i]=$(( ${ARM_N[$i]} + 1 ))
      POOL_SUM="$(fadd "$POOL_SUM" "$cost")"; POOL_N=$((POOL_N + 1))
    fi
    if [[ "$(jq -r '.status' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")" == "completed" ]]; then
      DONE[$i]=$(( ${DONE[$i]} + 1 ))
      log "done $jid ($(jq -r '"\(.arm) \(.fixture) t\(.trial) recall=\(([.graders[]? | select(.name=="recall-vs-defects.sh") | .details.recall][0]) // "n/a") \(.duration_ms/1000|floor)s"' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
    else
      FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
      log "FAILED $jid ($(jq -c '.error' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
    fi
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*
  else
    FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
    log "FAILED $jid (no row written; see $JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log)"
  fi
  write_status
}

#               [--max-usd <usd> [--run-cap <usd>]] [--screen [--screen-tasks N]]
#
# Spend cap (cycle-130 FR-2, SDD §5.5): --max-usd stops launching before the
#   next trial when spent + in_flight × run_cap + est_next > max, where spent =
#   the executor-reported total_cost_usd of this invocation's completed and
#   failed rows, run_cap = --run-cap (default evals.ablation.run_cap_usd in
#   .loa.config.yaml, else 12) reserved per running trial, and est_next = the
#   mean cost of this arm's completed trials (one task type per recall suite),
#   else the pooled mean, else the suite's ab.cost_hint (or cost_hint), else 5.0.
#   While the reservation alone blocks the launch it waits for a running trial;
#   when spent + est_next > max it cuts: no further launches, running trials
#   finish, STATUS.json gets cut_reason: max_usd and cut = {reason, spent,
#   in_flight_reserved, max, trials_launched, at_trial}, state partial, exit 1.
# Screen (bd-j4lwr): --screen runs one trial of the first N fixtures (default
#   2) per arm into <results-dir>/<suite>/screen-<UTC ts>/ (its own MANIFEST,
#   STATUS, rows), prints a per-arm table (trials, mean USD, mean recall) on
    [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]] && sleep 1
  done
  return 0
}

# est_next <arm> — the next trial's expected cost (see the header)
est_next() {
  local i; i="$(arm_index "$1")"
  if [[ "${ARM_N[$i]}" -gt 0 ]]; then awk -v s="${ARM_SUM[$i]}" -v n="${ARM_N[$i]}" 'BEGIN { printf "%.10g", s / n }'
  elif [[ "$POOL_N" -gt 0 ]]; then awk -v s="$POOL_SUM" -v n="$POOL_N" 'BEGIN { printf "%.10g", s / n }'
  else printf '%s' "$COST_HINT"; fi
}
# budget_gate <arm> <trial-number> — 0 launch; 1 cut (CUT_JSON set). Waits for a
# running trial while only the in-flight reservation blocks the launch.
budget_gate() {
  local arm="$1" at="$2" est inflight reserved
  while true; do
    est="$(est_next "$arm")"; inflight=${#PIDS[@]}
    reserved="$(awk -v k="$inflight" -v c="$RUN_CAP" 'BEGIN { printf "%.10g", k * c }')"
    if awk -v s="$SPENT" -v e="$est" -v m="$MAX_USD" 'BEGIN { exit !(s + e > m) }'; then
      CUT_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SPENT" --arg r "$reserved" --arg m "$MAX_USD" --arg e "$est" \
        --argjson launched "$LAUNCHED" --argjson at "$at" \
        '{reason: "max_usd", spent: ($s | tonumber), in_flight_reserved: ($r | tonumber), max: ($m | tonumber),
          est_next: ($e | tonumber), trials_launched: $launched, at_trial: $at}')"
      log "cut: max_usd $MAX_USD reached after $LAUNCHED trials (spent $SPENT, in-flight reserved $reserved, next est $est; trial $at not launched; reason recorded in STATUS.json)"
      return 1
    fi
    if awk -v s="$SPENT" -v r="$reserved" -v e="$est" -v m="$MAX_USD" 'BEGIN { exit !(s + r + e > m) }'; then
      reap "$inflight"; continue
    fi
    return 0
  done
}

n=0 LAUNCHED=0
for p in "${PLAN[@]}"; do
  IFS='|' read -r a f t <<<"$p"
  n=$((n + 1)); jid="$(printf 'j%04d' "$n")"
  reap "$CONCURRENCY"
  if [[ -n "$MAX_USD" ]] && ! budget_gate "$a" "$n"; then break; fi
  run_trial "$jid" "$a" "$f" "$t" &
  PIDS+=("$!"); PJOB+=("$jid"); PARM+=("$a")
  LAUNCHED=$((LAUNCHED + 1))
done
reap 1

#   no_gate_phases             no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record

#                              and FIX records, and every continuation's argv resumes it
#   gates_separate_sessions    REVIEW and AUDIT session ids are non-null, distinct from

#   effort_flag_medium         every argv carries --effort medium

I read all seven files in full. All 52 tests in `evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats` pass on a scratch copy run with jq 1.7.1, so the problems below are in places the tests don't reach. Nothing under `/workspace/pr` was modified, and the scratch copies are deleted.

The library header (`evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh`) matches its code for every function and toggle. I compared it against the base `execute-agent.sh` functions it was extracted from and found no behaviour regressions. The `pipeline-run.sh` header also matches the code on: the env allowlist, the pass-through keys, the docker flags, exactly two mounts, the exit-code mapping (124/137/143/129/130), the watchdog and cap math (`>=` against cap minus spent; `-ge` after each phase), and the BARE caps (30+60+2×40 = 170 turns, 15+25+2×15 = 70 minutes).

## Defects

1. **The driver runs the agent's git hooks and repo config on the host, which defeats the container — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:446-448` (`sgit`), called at `:783-787`.** High confidence.
   - The container mounts `sandbox/` read-write at `/workspace`, and that includes `sandbox/.git`.
   - After IMPLEMENT and after each FIX, the host driver runs `git add -A`, `git commit` and `git bundle` on that repo.
   - `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` don't block the repo's own `.git/config` (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`) or `.git/hooks/*`.
   - I reproduced it with the exact `sgit` environment: a planted `.git/hooks/pre-commit` ran on the host and wrote a file.
   - Possible fix: pass `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false`, or keep the git dir outside the mount (`--git-dir` under `meta/`).

2. **The driver copies files the agent can replace with symlinks — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:773-774, 777`.** Medium-high confidence.
   - The plain `cp` of `sandbox/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl`, `sandbox/.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl` and `grimoires/.../adversarial-*.json` into `eval/` follows symlinks.
   - In container mode the agent can point these at absolute host paths. The host driver then copies host files into the run's `eval/` artefacts.

3. **The pricing cache never works — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:577-597`, called at `:718`.** High confidence.
   - `price_for` is only ever called as `prices="$(price_for "$model")"`, which runs in a subshell, so the `PRICE_CACHE=` assignment at `:595` is thrown away.
   - Result: `pricing.py` runs again for every phase, contradicting the header's "fetched once per model" (`:91`) and "one lookup per model" (`:576`).

4. **Codex version in the header contradicts the Dockerfile — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:85` vs `evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:25`.** High confidence that they disagree; I can't tell which is intended.
   - The header says "codex 0.137.0 by Dockerfile.ablation", but the image pins `ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1`.
   - The header uses this to claim `image_digest` identifies the batch's versions.

5. **A dead beads build stage contradicts the Dockerfile's own comment — `evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:19-20` vs `:82-84`.** Medium confidence.
   - Lines 19-20 build `cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6`, but no `COPY --from=brbuild` ever uses it.
   - Lines 82-84 say "No beads (br) in the image: beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io".
   - If that comment is right, the classic (non-BuildKit) builder fails the whole image build. The node-digest comment at `:17-18` also now sits above the unpinned `rust:1-bookworm` FROM.

6. **Container-mode launch failures are misreported as agent errors — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:860-862` (the in-container CLI is never checked; `:426` checks host mode only).** Medium confidence.
   - The header (`:99-100`) says a missing CLI/docker is exit 2 (infrastructure).
   - In container mode, a missing in-image `claude` (exit 127), a docker daemon or name-conflict error (125), or 126 all land in the generic `rc != 0` branch. They become `agent_error`, exit 1.

7. **`--help` output is cut off — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:153`.** Medium confidence.
   - `sed -n '2,105p' "$0"` stops mid-sentence at line 105 ("…so a SIGKILLed driver leaves a").
   - The header runs to line 117, so help drops the rest of that sentence plus the Env and Mount library sections.

## Lower-severity notes

- **Snapshot key case — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:50` vs `:788`.** The header documents `index.json` as `{IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2: commit}`, but the code writes lowercase keys (`implement`, `fix1`). The tests and `ablation-row.sh` expect lowercase, so only the doc is wrong.
- **`.claude/` code in the trusted harness — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:586`.** The driver executes `$REPO_ROOT/.claude/adapters/.../pricing.py`, which sits awkwardly with the trust-boundary comment at `:125-126` and with the library's reason for using hashlib.
- **jq ≥ 1.7 is silently required — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:704-708, 816-826, 881-882, 224-225`.**
  - Under jq 1.6, `{label: $label}` doesn't compile, so every run aborts as infrastructure_error.
  - Separately, `split("\u0000") | .[:-1]` drops the last real argv/env entry, e.g. the `medium` after `--effort`.
  - Nothing checks or documents the version.
- **Hidden-directory check differs from the scan — `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:455`.** The fixture check is case-sensitive (`*/hidden/*`) while the later scan (`:503-504`) is case-insensitive, and review-catch fixtures skip this check entirely.
- **Test stub diverges from the real library — `evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:24, 89`.**
  - It prints `mount=whole_tree` where the real library prints `mount=tree`, and `evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:245` asserts `whole_tree`.
  - Its `check_fixture_path_rule` misses dangling symlinks (`-e` only, while the real one also checks `-L`).
  - So that test checks the stub, not the shipped contract.

sgit() {  # git on the sandbox repo, isolated from the operator's git config
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$META" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 LC_ALL=C \
    git -C "$WS" "$@"
}

  ledger_micro="$(printf '%s\n' "$ledger_rows" | jq -R -n '[inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object")
        | (.cost_micro_usd // ((.cost_usd // 0) * 1000000))] | add // 0 | round' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  minv_after="$(wc -l < "$WS/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')"
  cp "$WS/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl" "$EVALD/model-invoke.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
  cp "$WS/.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl" "$EVALD/cost-ledger.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
  local env_f
  for env_f in "$WS"/grimoires/loa/a2a/"$SPRINT"/adversarial-*.json; do
    [[ -f "$env_f" ]] && cp "$env_f" "$EVALD/"
  done
  if [[ $rc -eq 124 ]] || { [[ $rc -eq 137 ]] && [[ $elapsed_ms -ge $(( tsec * 1000 )) ]]; }; then timed_out=true; fi

  local snap="" verdict=null skill effort_req
  if [[ "$INTERRUPTED" -eq 0 ]] && { [[ "$name" == IMPLEMENT ]] || [[ "$name" == FIX ]]; }; then
    sgit add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $label" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    snap="$(sgit rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$snap" ]]; then
      sgit bundle create "$SNAPS/$label.bundle" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      SNAPSHOTS_JSON="$(jq -c --arg k "$(printf '%s' "$label" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" --arg v "$snap" '.[$k] = $v' <<<"$SNAPSHOTS_JSON")"
      jq -n --argjson s "$SNAPSHOTS_JSON" --arg base "$BASE_COMMIT" '$s + {base: $base}' > "$SNAPS/index.json"
    fi
[[ "$EXECUTOR" == container ]] && make_home

# --- pricing (one lookup per model; D-4.10) ---------------------------------------------
PRICE_CACHE=""
price_for() {  # price_for <model id> → {"in":…,"out":…,"cr":…,"cc":…} micro-USD per Mtok, or null
  local m="$1" hit alias j
  hit="$(printf '%s\n' "$PRICE_CACHE" | awk -F'\t' -v m="$m" '$1 == m {print $2; exit}')"
  [[ -n "$hit" ]] && { printf '%s' "$hit"; return 0; }
  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON:-}" ]]; then

head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:447 — sgit runs `git add -A`/`commit`/`bundle` on the host (called at :783-787) against sandbox/.git, which the agent can write to (mounted rw at /workspace in container mode); GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/NOSYSTEM do not neutralise the repo's own .git/config (core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor) or .git/hooks/*, so a planted pre-commit hook runs on the host and the container boundary is defeated; pass `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false` or keep the git dir outside the mount.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:773 — the host driver uses plain `cp` (here, :774 and :777) to copy sandbox/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl, cost-ledger.jsonl and adversarial-*.json, which the agent controls; cp follows symlinks, so an agent-planted symlink pulls arbitrary host files into the run's eval/ artefacts (and into the cost/row evidence).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:595 — the PRICE_CACHE assignment is lost because price_for is only called through command substitution (`prices="$(price_for "$model")"` at :718, a subshell); pricing.py runs again for every phase, contradicting "fetched once per model" (:91) and "one lookup per model" (:576).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:85 — the header says Dockerfile.ablation pins codex 0.137.0, but Dockerfile.ablation:25 pins CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1; the doc uses this to claim image_digest identifies the batch's toolchain versions.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:153 — `--help` prints `sed -n '2,105p'`, which stops mid-sentence ("…so a SIGKILLed driver leaves a"); the header runs to about line 117, so the Env and mount-library sections never print.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:860 — in container mode, a missing in-image claude (127), a docker daemon or name-conflict error (125) or 126 all fall into the generic rc != 0 branch and are recorded as agent_error (exit 1); the header (:99-100) documents a missing CLI/docker/image as infrastructure (exit 2), and the CLI preflight at :426 only covers host mode.
head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:19 — dead `brbuild` stage: `cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6` is never used by any `COPY --from=brbuild`, and lines 82-84 say beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io, so under a non-BuildKit builder this stage fails the whole image build; the pinned-digest comment at :17-18 also now sits above an unpinned `rust:1-bookworm` FROM.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266 — integrity_clean never FAILs when arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 (the sha of checksums.json at mount time) differs from the current sandbox checksums.json; it only drops the "(matches checksums.json)" suffix. An agent that edits a .claude file and rewrites its manifest entry (or adds unlisted files) still passes, so the rule does not prove integrity.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:87 — the dissent envelope is read from the agent-writable sandbox first and from the driver-copied eval/ only as a fallback, so an agent-written adversarial-*.json can satisfy one_voice_planned; this contradicts the header's "evidence from run artefacts, never from what the agent said" (:8-10).
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:201 — same precedence problem as took-effect.sh: the sandbox envelope wins over eval/, so the agent can spoof voices_run and the envelope-driven degraded cause in the row.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:247 — model_mismatches flags every models_used key other than model_requested; models_used (pipeline-run.sh:830) is the CLI's full modelUsage map, which routinely includes helper models such as haiku (execute-agent.sh:371-373 notes this), so ordinary runs are marked degraded. Also, `keys` on a non-object models_used aborts jq with exit 5, outside the documented 0/1/2 exit codes.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:224 — run-sized JSON ($PIPE_JSON, $MINV built from the whole model-invoke.jsonl, the envelopes, $DOT_WRITES) is passed as --argjson arguments, which hit Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit (MAX_ARG_STRLEN); a long run's model-invoke.jsonl makes jq fail with "Argument list too long" (exit 126). Use --slurpfile or --rawfile instead.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:230 — ms() calls fromdateiso8601 with no guard; a timestamp with an offset (e.g. +00:00) or an empty string aborts the row writer with jq exit 5 instead of a documented exit code.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:506 — the --max-usd cap charges failed or timed-out trials only their reported total_cost_usd (`// 0`), and the no-row branch at :521-523 charges nothing; runaway trials that die without reporting a cost (possibly close to run_cap each) never move SPENT, so the batch keeps launching past the cap. Charge run_cap for trials with no reported cost.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:391 — the suite aggregate excludes batches by directory name (`! -path "$SUITE_DIR/screen-*"`), but a non-screen `--batch screen-foo` passes the name check at :167, so results of a real batch with that name silently drop out of the suite STATUS.json; filter on the batch's screen marker, or refuse screen-* names without --screen.

content.text:
I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 22 findings, and the verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Three parallel reviewers split the scripts. I checked the main claims myself, and the reviewers ran the bats suites on scratch copies outside `pr/`, which I left unchanged. Those suites pass, apart from two tests that need repo files not included in the PR. So the defects below are in paths the tests don't cover.

**What blocks the merge:**
- **Host code execution from the sandbox (`pipeline-run.sh:447`):** after IMPLEMENT and each FIX, the host driver runs `git add`, `git commit` and `git bundle` on `sandbox/.git`, which the agent can write to. The repo's own hooks and `core.fsmonitor` are not disabled, so a hook the agent plants runs on the host. That defeats the container. One reviewer reproduced it.
- **Symlink copies (`pipeline-run.sh:773`):** the driver copies agent-controlled ledger and envelope files with plain `cp`, which follows symlinks. An agent can pull host files into the run's evidence.
- **The integrity check proves less than it claims (`took-effect.sh:266`):** if the recorded manifest hash no longer matches the sandbox `checksums.json`, the rule still passes. An agent that edits a `.claude` file and rewrites its manifest entry still gets `integrity_clean OK`.
- **Evidence the agent can spoof (`took-effect.sh:87`, `ablation-row.sh:201`):** the dissent envelopes are read from the sandbox first and from the driver-copied `eval/` only as a fallback.
- **CI gaps (`bats-tests.yml`):**
  - The trigger path filters don't include `evals/**` or the new `tools/` scripts, so the new steps don't run on most of this PR's changes.
  - The PR edits tracked `.claude/` files without regenerating `.claude/checksums.json`. I expect the new `gen-checksums.sh --check` gate to fail on this PR itself. I couldn't run it here because the manifest isn't in the PR snapshot.

**Correctness problems:**
- **Spend cap leak (`run-arms.sh:506`):** `--max-usd` charges nothing for trials that die without reporting a cost, so a batch can keep launching past its cap.
- **Rows marked `degraded` (`ablation-row.sh:247`):** any helper model in `modelUsage`, such as a haiku call, flags the row.
- **Row writer crashes (`ablation-row.sh:224`, `:230`):** large run data passed through `--argjson` hits Linux's per-argument limit, and an unguarded timestamp parse aborts on offset timestamps. Both exit outside the documented codes.
- **Pricing cache never works (`pipeline-run.sh:595`):** it is filled inside a subshell, so pricing is looked up again on every phase.
- **Container failures misreported (`pipeline-run.sh:860`):** a missing CLI or docker error in container mode is recorded as an agent error rather than an infrastructure error.
- **Screen-batch filter (`run-arms.sh:391`):** a normal batch named `screen-*` silently drops out of the suite totals.
- **Path quoting (`check-manifest-paths.sh:80`):** it disagrees with `gen-checksums.sh` on paths with non-ASCII characters or quotes, and reports them as untracked.

**Docs and tests:**
- The codex version in the `pipeline-run.sh` header doesn't match the Dockerfile.
- `--help` output stops mid-sentence.
- The Dockerfile has a dead beads build stage that its own comment says can't build.
- `gen-checksums.bats` is missing the GC-8 test its header names.
- Two assertions in `freeze.bats` check nothing.
- `spend.bats` SP-6 is too weak to catch a broken suite-file read.
- The mount stub reports a different value from the real library, and a test pins the stub's value.

One reviewer reported that these files match a public upstream commit and that later upstream commits fixed several of these issues. I didn't verify that; it doesn't affect the findings.
